These effects were associated with changes in cortical SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1 expression, together with alterations in NF-κB- and Keap1/Nrf2-related protein levels. AKBA administration was also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, and exploratory correlation analyses suggested associations between selected bacterial taxa and cortical protein expression. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that concurrent AKBA administration provides protection against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction, potentially involving coordinated changes in inflammatory, antioxidant, and neurotrophic responses. However, the causal roles of the candidate proteins and gut microbiota alterations remain to be established through further functional investigations.

articles.title: Mechanisms involved in the sex-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration induced by MDMA in a mouse model of adolescent drug exposure.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA, or "ecstasy") is an amphetamine-related drug mainly used by adolescents. Studies in mice have demonstrated that MDMA administration induces toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, some of which may be sex- and age-dependent. Since adolescence is a critical period for brain development, this study aimed to investigate some of the mechanisms underlying MDMA-induced toxicity in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system of adolescent mice. METHODS: Male and female adolescent mice were treated with a regimen of MDMA (4 × 20 mg/kg, 2 h apart) that has previously been demonstrated to induce toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system. After treatment, mice were sacrificed at different time points (i.e., 30, 60 or 120 min) to evaluate loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons, antioxidant and proteasome activity, reactive radical species (RRS) and neurodegeneration-related proteins. Immunohistochemistry for tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was performed in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). Moreover, midbrains were evaluated for: i) activity of the antioxidant enzymes glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) 1 and 2 of the proteolytic subunits β2 trypsin-like and β5 chymotrypsin-like of the proteasome system; ii) expression of SOD1 and SOD2 genes; iii) presence of RRS and iv) phosphorylation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK1/2) and of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). RESULTS: Male mice displayed: i) decreased TH immunoreactivity and cresyl violet staining (120 min after the last MDMA administration); ii) reduced activity of SOD and β2 trypsin-like proteasome subunit, both in basal conditions and 120 min after the last MDMA administration; iii) increase in p-ERK1/2 (30 min after the last MDMA administration). Female mice treated with MDMA displayed: i) decreased SOD1 and SOD2 gene expression and ii) increased GPx activity (both observed 120 min after the last MDMA administration). CONCLUSION: MDMA treatment during adolescence altered the homeostasis of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system in both male and female mice. Adolescent male mice treated with MDMA appeared more sensitive to dysfunction in proteasome and ERK1/2 activation. Conversely, female mice efficiently maintained the antioxidant activity, which could contrast the neurotoxic effects of MDMA on the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.

articles.title: Comparable TXNIP-inhibiting, anti-apoptotic and anti-diabetic effects of TIX100 and its individual enantiomers.
articles.abstract: Thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) is a stress-responsive gene that is upregulated by endoplasmic reticulum stress, cytokine toxicity and high glucose and pathologically elevated in diabetes. In pancreatic islets this leads to dysfunction and promotes beta cell apoptosis thereby contributing to disease progression. On the other hand, targeting inhibition of beta cell TXNIP has emerged as a promising, novel, therapeutic approach for type 1 diabetes. Indeed, genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of TXNIP protect against beta cell destruction and diabetes. TIX100 is an oral, small molecule TXNIP inhibitor currently completing Phase 1 clinical trials. Structurally, TIX100 is a chiral drug and thus far has been used as a racemate. Even though the effects of a racemate and its isolated enantiomers can vary greatly providing potential advantages for drug development, the properties of the individual TIX100 enantiomers have remained unknown. The aim of the current studies was therefore to elucidate how the individual TIX100 enantiomers compare to the TIX100 racemate. Using in vitro and in vivo studies in diabetic mice, we found that the TIX100 racemate and its individual R- and S-enantiomers are stable, have similar metabolic profiles and are comparable in potency and effectiveness of lowering beta cell TXNIP, promoting beta cell survival and function and protecting against beta cell destruction-induced diabetes. Taken together with the extensive preclinical work and the Phase 1 clinical trials using the TIX100 racemate that have not revealed any relevant safety concerns, no rationale for pursuing a single enantiomer for further diabetes drug development seems to exist in the case of TIX100.

articles.title: Diterpenoid tanshinones enhance CD8+ T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity in gastric cancer by suppressing ENO1 activity and glycolysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge contains bioactive tanshinones with antitumor activity, but whether diterpenoid tanshinones (DT) suppress gastric cancer by coupling glycolytic inhibition to CD8+ T-cell responses remains unclear. This study investigated the antitumor effects of DT and the contribution of the ENO1-lactate axis to tumor immune regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: DT composition was characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. Antitumor activity was evaluated in a subcutaneous syngeneic MFC gastric cancer model in 615 mice, including CD8+ T-cell depletion and lactate-challenge experiments. Tumor-infiltrating immune cells were analyzed by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. In gastric cancer cells, lactate production and extracellular acidification were measured using colorimetric and Seahorse assays. Network pharmacology, drug affinity responsive target stability, and cellular thermal shift assays were used to identify and assess candidate targets, followed by western blotting and enzyme-activity assays. RESULTS: DT suppressed tumor growth and increased intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration, whereas CD8+ T-cell depletion attenuated its antitumor effect. DT reduced lactate production and glycolytic activity in gastric cancer cells and tumors. DARTS and CETSA supported target engagement between DT and ENO1. DT reduced ENO1 enzymatic activity and phosphoenolpyruvate levels without markedly changing ENO1 protein abundance. Exogenous lactate promoted tumor growth, while acidic culture conditions reduced CD8+ T-cell viability. Compared with the model group, DT alone increased the percentages of CD8+ and GZMB + cells and decreased the percentage of PD-1+ cells in tumor tissue. CONCLUSION: DT restrains gastric tumor growth through an immunometabolic mechanism involving ENO1 inhibition, reduced glycolytic lactate production, and antitumor activity involving CD8+ T cells. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of DT and the ENO1-lactate axis in gastric cancer.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of antiseizure medication dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States: A retrospective claims-based cohort study, 2004-2021.
articles.abstract: AIM: To describe trends and identify factors associated with antiseizure medications (ASMs) dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective claims-based cohort study within AMerican PREGNANcy Mother-Child CohorT (AM-PREGNANT). We identified pregnant persons aged 15-45 years continuously enrolled from 12 months before the last menstrual period (LMP) through pregnancy end, with ≥1 ASM dispensing from 2004 to 2021. Annual prevalence of ASM dispensing was estimated by pregnancy start year. Within a first-ever ASM dispensing cohort, we examined dispensing patterns across pregnancy time windows, ASM-related indications and changes in dispensing during pregnancy. We also assessed factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP among those initiating ASM therapy before pregnancy. RESULTS: The cohort included 337 449 pregnant persons. Annual ASM dispensing prevalence remained stable (10%-13%). Among those with first-ever ASM dispensing (n = 115 896), 56% had dispensing before pregnancy, of whom 65% had no dispensing during pregnancy. The most common starting ASMs were clonazepam (28%), topiramate (25%) and gabapentin (20%). Dispensing patterns varied by indication: epilepsy was characterized by lamotrigine, levetiracetam and topiramate, generally dispensed for >60 days, whereas psychiatric and pain indications showed more variable patterns, typically with <30 days of dispensing. Factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP included pre-specified indications, comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing; among these, epilepsy/seizure had the strongest association (aOR 2.14; 95% CI 1.78-2.59). CONCLUSIONS: ASM dispensing varied by indication, with most pre-pregnancy dispensing not continuing during pregnancy. Epilepsy/seizure was most strongly associated with dispensing at LMP, with additional associations observed for comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing.

articles.title: The RARγ antagonist CD2665 attenuates ATRA-induced growth plate impairment by preserving chondrocyte homeostasis.
articles.abstract: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)-based therapy is clinically important but may cause skeletal toxicity during development. The contribution of retinoic acid receptor γ (RARγ) to ATRA-associated growth plate injury remains unclear. This study investigated whether the RARγ antagonist CD2665 attenuates ATRA-induced growth plate impairment and whether it compromises ATRA-induced responses in HL-60 cells. Juvenile Sprague-Dawley rats were treated with vehicle, ATRA, ATRA plus CD2665, or CD2665. Skeletal growth, growth plate morphology, RAR subtype expression, chondrocyte fate-related markers, apoptosis-related proteins, and IHH-GLI1 protein expression were assessed. Primary growth plate chondrocytes were used to evaluate viability, proliferation, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, and related proteins, while HL-60 cells were used to assess ATRA-induced growth inhibition and myeloid differentiation. ATRA selectively decreased RARγ immunoreactivity among RAR subtypes in the growth plate, reduced skeletal growth and growth plate height, altered growth plate zonal architecture, and decreased IHH and GLI1 protein expression in tissues and primary chondrocytes. CD2665 partially attenuated these abnormalities and improved selected chondrocyte fate-related markers. CD2665 also reduced ATRA-associated Annexin V positivity in primary chondrocytes, although its effects on BAX and BCL-2 were limited. In HL-60 cells, CD2665 did not compromise ATRA-induced growth inhibition, G0/G1-phase accumulation, maturation-associated morphology, or CD11b/CD14 upregulation. These findings indicate that CD2665 partially attenuates ATRA-induced growth retardation and growth plate impairment, in association with preservation of IHH and GLI1 protein expression and partial improvement of chondrocyte fate-related changes, without obvious compromise of ATRA-induced differentiation-associated responses in HL-60 cells under the present experimental conditions.

articles.title: Retrospective assessment of AAV empty/full capsid methods using real-world analytical data.
articles.abstract: Due to incomplete packaging efficiency of recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV), analytical methods are required to characterize capsid populations. Here, we retrospectively evaluated seven years of analytical development data generated using the standalone methods of analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC), negative-stain transmission electron microscopy (TEM), anion-exchange UV-ratio analysis (ACUVRA) and mass photometry, as well as genome-to-capsid ratio (G/C) estimates derived from separate genome and capsid titer methods. The dataset included multiple capsids, products, processes, and sample matrices. The standalone methods showed strong correlations across the historical dataset, although absolute values differed because of method-specific differences in analytical resolution, capsid species coverage, reporting units, and underlying assumptions. Genome-to-capsid ratio showed weaker relationships with the standalone methods, reflecting compounded assay variability and program-specific factors. These observations informed a fit-for-purpose strategy for deploying empty/full characterization methods across process development, product characterization, and release-support activities.

articles.title: Metformin mitigates trophoblast GLUT1 inhibition through HIF-1α/Fibronectin/AMPK pathway in preeclampsia.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a complex gestational hypertensive disorder associated with dysregulated placental energy metabolism, and fibronectin (FN) plays a critical role in its development. Although metformin has shown potential in reducing the risk of PE, its effects on FN and trophoblast glucose transport regulation remain unclear. In this study, experiments were conducted using FN-pretreated and FN-knockdown HTR-8/SVneo cells, clinical placental specimens, and a preeclampsia mouse model. Aberrant FN and GLUT1 expression was observed in human preeclamptic placentas. Under hypoxic conditions, FN and GLUT1 were upregulated in two trophoblastic cell lines (HTR-8/SVneo and JAR) and in primary placental cells. However, exogenous FN suppressed hypoxia-associated GLUT1 upregulation, reduced extracellular L-lactate levels, and impaired trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. These effects were associated with activation of AMPK signaling. Metformin reduced HIF-1α, FN, and phosphorylated AMPK levels in FN-treated trophoblasts under hypoxia, while increasing GLUT1 expression and extracellular L-lactate levels and restoring trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. Notably, metformin increased AMPK phosphorylation in FN-silenced cells, suggesting that its effects on AMPK signaling depend, at least partly, on FN status. In the mouse model, increased placental FN was accompanied by altered GLUT1 expression, impaired primary cilia formation, and changes in AMPK-related signaling. Metformin treatment improved maternal blood pressure and fetal growth, reduced placental FN levels, and increased GLUT1 expression and ciliogenesis. In conclusion, FN disrupts trophoblast function under hypoxia and is associated with changes in GLUT1 expression and lactate output, involving AMPK signaling. Metformin alleviates these dysfunctions by suppressing FN and reversing FN-mediated GLUT1 inhibition and AMPK activation. These findings identify the HIF-1α/FN/AMPK axis as a critical mechanism in PE pathophysiology and support the potential repurposing of metformin for PE prevention.

articles.title: The evaluation of the potential application of friedelin as an alternative to estrogen in an ovariectomized rat model.
articles.abstract: Menopause is a condition where ovaries stop functioning due to a decrease in hormonal levels (estrogen). It leads to loss of fertility, hot flashes, anxiety, and vaginal dryness. It is recommended to take hormonal therapy to escape from these problems. Although hormonal therapy has some benefits, there are severe health-related risks like cardiovascular disease and ovarian cancer. These problems forced to search for safer alternatives like phytoestrogen. The objective of this study was to test the efficacy of friedelin as an estrogen. Friedelin is a plant-derived triterpenoid compound. Ovariectomized rats were given friedelin for 28 days, and after that behavioral parameters were recorded along with other analyses like serum estradiol level estimation, uterine histology, and deciduoma formation. Estradiol-driven gene expression (mRNA and protein level) was also checked, along with immunofluorescence localization; these genes were estrogen receptor alpha (ER-α), estrogen receptor beta (ER-β), complement component 3 (C3), early growth response 1(EgR1), and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA). Progesterone-like activity of friedelin was also checked. Improved behavioural responses were recorded, with significant increases in serum estradiol levels and epithelium thickness along with increased endometrial gland numbers. The significant upregulation of estrogen-responsive genes was found at the mRNA and protein levels in friedelin-treated groups. The localization of these genes was found primarily in endometrial stroma, luminal, and glandular epithelium. Deciduoma formation occurred only in the progesterone-administered group which denies friedelin's progesterone-like activity. The friedelin showed estrogen-like activity. Further, preclinical and clinical investigations are needed to establish friedelin's safety and efficacy for medical applications.

articles.title: Single-cell transcriptome-based identification of core keratinocyte biomarkers and targeted drug discovery for atopic dermatitis.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disorder driven by epidermal barrier impairment and keratinocyte dysfunction. Current therapies are limited by insufficient target specificity and high recurrence rates. This study aimed to identify keratinocyte-derived biomarkers and develop novel targeted agents for precise diagnosis and treatment of AD. Single-cell RNA sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to screen for key AD biomarkers, and machine learning algorithms with ROC curve analysis were applied to evaluate their diagnostic performance. Immunohistochemistry confirmed LYPD3 protein upregulation in AD lesional skin. In silico knockdown simulations at single-cell resolution elucidated LYPD3-mediated signaling pathways. Structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations identified candidate LYPD3-targeted compounds, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) validated target engagement and direct binding. An in vitro keratinocyte inflammation model and an in vivo MC903 (calcipotriol)-induced AD mouse model were established to assess therapeutic efficacy. LYPD3, KRT6C, and FABP5 were specifically overexpressed in AD keratinocytes, showed excellent diagnostic performance that was validated in a fully independent external cohort, and correlated closely with cutaneous immune infiltration. LYPD3 depletion disrupted epidermal barrier integrity and keratinocyte differentiation pathways. CETSA confirmed target engagement, and BLI demonstrated direct binding between Rebastinib and LYPD3. Rebastinib inhibited keratinocyte hyperproliferation and inflammation in vitro and significantly ameliorated epidermal lesions while suppressing Th2-type inflammatory responses in AD mice. These findings identify three keratinocyte-specific AD biomarkers and support Rebastinib as a promising LYPD3-targeted therapeutic candidate, offering new insights into precision diagnosis and targeted therapy of AD.

articles.title: Proteomics identifies FMNL1 as a therapeutic target for intestinal barrier repair in obesity-associated chronic diarrhea.
articles.abstract: An increasing number of studies have identified a positive association between obesity and chronic diarrhea, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We conducted quantitative proteomics on ileum tissues from obese people with chronic diarrhea (OD, n = 23), obese people without chronic diarrhea (OB, n = 8), and healthy controls (Control, n = 9). Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in the OD vs. Control and OD vs. OB comparisons were significantly enriched in pathways related to macrophage cytokine production. Notably, down-regulated DEPs in OD vs. OB comparison were associated with mucin type O-glycan biosynthesis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified 56 common DEPs, with formin-like protein 1 (FMNL1) emerging as a key candidate through machine learning algorithms. FMNL1, a component of macrophage podosomes, was significantly upregulated in OD patients, as validated by Western blot and co-immunofluorescence staining. Functionally, FMNL1 knockdown ameliorated palmitic acid-induced proinflammatory cytokine expression in THP-1-derived macrophages and improved tight junctions in the Caco-2/ THP-1 co-culture model. Collectively, our results suggest FMNL1 as a crucial role in OD pathogenesis through mediating macrophage inflammation, providing a molecular rationale for targeted therapeutic strategies in obesity-associated diarrhea.

articles.title: Sitagliptin mitigates ferroptosis induced by severe acute pancreatitis through gut microbiota improvement and activation of Nrf2 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) represents a critical clinical syndrome with high morbidity and mortality, in which gut microbiota dysbiosis plays a pivotal role in disease progression. Here, we investigated the modulatory effects of sitagliptin (SIT) on microbiota alterations associated with SAP and explored the underlying mechanisms. Using SAP mouse models with or without microbiota depletion, fecal 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that SAP-induced dysbiosis was closely associated with ferroptosis-related pathways, accompanied by decreased GPX4 and Nrf2 expression. SIT treatment restored microbial homeostasis, alleviated intestinal barrier injury, and inhibited ferroptosis via activation of Nrf2 signaling. In LPS-treated Caco2 cells, SIT similarly attenuated ferroptosis-related changes, including lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress. Collectively, SIT protects against SAP by reshaping gut microbiota and suppressing ferroptosis through the Nrf2 pathway, providing insights for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rh1 alleviates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury via macrophage polarization and ERK pathway modulation.
articles.abstract: Inflammation plays a crucial role in the early stages of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (MI/R) injury, with macrophages being key contributors to this process. Ginsenoside Rh1 (G-Rh1) is a danmarane-based tetracyclic triterpenoid saponin found in plants of the genus Panax, such as ginseng and Panax notoginseng. G-Rh1 can be absorbed by the human body and is beneficial for protecting the heart and has anti-inflammatory effects. This study established rat model of MI/R induced by ligation of the left anterior descending artery, and administered G-Rh1 and the positive drug diltiazem (DTZ) by gavage. The results showed that G-Rh1 treatment could reduce the area of myocardial infarction, improve cardiac function, alleviate myocardial inflammatory infiltration and pathological damage. In addition, in the G-Rh1 treatment group, the M1-type macrophage marker was significantly down-regulated, while the M2-type macrophage marker was significantly up-regulated. G-Rh1 may exert protective effects on myocardial tissue in association with regulation of macrophage polarization. Meanwhile, G-Rh1 inhibited the activation of the ERK pathway after LPS-induced polarization of macrophages. In RAW264.7 macrophages, G-Rh1 reduced the mRNA expression levels of M1-type biomarkers induced by LPS and reduced the number of M1-type macrophages. Interestingly, under LPS stimulation, G-Rh1 inhibited the activation of ERK pathway and the polarization of M1 macrophages, corresponding with reduced production of inflammatory cytokines. In summary, these findings indicate that the cardioprotective effect of G-Rh1 is associated with the reduction of M1-polarized macrophages, the increase of M2-polarized macrophages and the inhibition of the ERK signaling pathway. This effect subsequently alleviates inflammation caused by MI/R and improves cardiac dysfunction.

articles.title: Hyodeoxycholic acid inhibits cholesterol gallstone formation by regulating hepatic Atpif1 induced mitochondria-cholesterol metabolism.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigated the role of hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA) in preventing cholesterol gallstones (CGs) formation by regulating the hepatic ATPase inhibitory factor 1 (Atpif1). METHODS: We observed significantly elevated hepatic Atpif1 expression in gallstone patients and CG mice, which was associated with suppressed tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle activity, impaired mitophagy, and increased hepatic cholesterol accumulation. Human transcriptomic data (GSE7117) further supported clinical relevance: Atpif1 expression decreased in liver of gallstone patients after dietary intervention. HDCA dose-dependently reduced gallstone burden and hepatic lipid deposition in mice, concomitant with reduction of hepatic Atpif1, restoration of TCA enzymes expression, enhancement of mitochondrial respiration and mitophagy, and upregulation of bile acid (BA) synthases. Atpif1 knockout (KO) mice confirmed this mechanism. Similar to HDCA treatment, Atpif1 deficiency decreased gallstone burden, improved lipid homeostasis, and increased BA synthesis. Mechanistically, inhibition of Atpif1 alleviated the suppression of ATP synthase activity, enhancing oxidative phosphorylation, and redirecting acetyl-CoA flux toward TCA cycle and away from de novo cholesterol synthesis. RESULTS: Consequently, acetyl-CoA was transferred from cholesterol synthesis to oxidative metabolism, reducing cholesterol accumulation in liver. By relieving Atpif1-mediated inhibition of ATP synthase, HDCA increased ATP turnover and TCA cycle demand, which competitively depleted the shared acetyl-CoA pool required for cholesterol synthesis. Consistent with this, ADP-treated hepatocytes showed reduced de novo cholesterol synthesis. CONCLUSION: Collectively, HDCA inhibits CG formation partly by suppressing hepatic Atpif1, coordinately reducing cholesterol synthesis and increasing cholesterol-to-BA conversion, thereby effectively preventing cholesterol supersaturation. Atpif1 was identified as a possible therapeutic target that links mitochondrial dysfunction to CG pathogenesis.

articles.title: Sauchinone protects against pathological cardiac hypertrophy by targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major contributor to heart failure and remains insufficiently targeted by current therapies that primarily focus on hemodynamic regulation rather than underlying molecular mechanisms. Sauchinone, a bioactive lignan isolated from Saururus chinensis, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects. However, its role in pathological cardiac hypertrophy and the associated mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of sauchinone on pathological cardiac hypertrophy and to elucidate its potential mechanism. The H9c2, a rat cardiomyocyte cell line, along with human embryonic stem cells-derived cardiomyocytes (hESC-CMs), were employed to investigate the therapeutic potential of sauchinone on angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced hypertrophy in vitro. An established mouse model of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced cardiac hypertrophy model were used for the animal studies. The investigation combined proteomics with molecular docking to explore the mechanisms by which sauchinone influences pathological cardiac hypertrophy. Sauchinone significantly attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, as evidenced by reduced cell size and decreased expression of hypertrophic markers in both H9c2 cells and hESC-CMs. In vivo, sauchinone markedly improved cardiac structure and function, reduced myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis, and restored systolic and diastolic function in HCM and TAC mice. Mechanistically, quantitative proteomics and pathway enrichment analyses revealed that sauchinone significantly inhibited the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB signaling pathways, which was further confirmed by reduced phosphorylation of key pathway components. Notably, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and target engagement assays demonstrated that sauchinone directly interacts with cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), suggesting a dual-target mechanism. Collectively, these findings indicate that sauchinone alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by coordinately suppressing inflammatory and growth signaling pathways via targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt axes. Sauchinone may therefore represent a promising multi-target therapeutic candidate for the treatment of pathological cardiac hypertrophy.

articles.title: Carboplatin tissue pharmacokinetics following intraperitoneal and systemic treatment: a microdialysis porcine study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Understanding carboplatin's tissue pharmacokinetics is critical for assessing its locoregional potential in Hyperthermic and Normothermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC, NIPEC) in ovarian cancer. This study assessed carboplatin exposure in tissues associated with ovarian cancer carcinomatosis across clinically relevant treatment regimens, using microdialysis in a healthy porcine model. METHODS: Animals were divided into three groups receiving HIPEC, NIPEC, or intravenous (IV) carboplatin. A minor cytoreductive surgery was performed in the HIPEC and NIPEC groups, followed by carboplatin perfusion (800 mg/m2). The IV group received a 30 min carboplatin infusion (625 mg). Unbound carboplatin concentrations were measured by microdialysis at intra-abdominal target sites during and after chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was parietal peritoneum AUC0-∞ between groups. KEY RESULTS: Parietal peritoneal AUC0-∞ was higher after HIPEC than after IV treatment (geometric mean ratio 2.37; 95% CI 1.08-5.17), whereas the NIPEC-IV (1.61; 0.73-3.53) and the exploratory HIPEC-NIPEC (1.47; 0.58-3.73) comparisons were inconclusive. Omental exposure showed a similar numerical pattern. IV treatment showed numerically higher exposure in plasma, rectum, liver, and superficial stomach. Perfusate carboplatin concentration decreased by approximately 32%. Greater inter-individual variability was evident following intraperitoneal chemotherapy. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: The intraperitoneal regimens achieved numerically higher carboplatin exposure in the peritoneal lining than the IV regimen, with lower systemic exposure but greater variability. The study was not powered to determine whether hyperthermia affects carboplatin pharmacokinetics. These findings may inform further development and clinical evaluation of intraperitoneal carboplatin chemotherapy in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Gastroprotective Effect of Petasites japonicus Ethanol Extract Against HCl/Ethanol-Induced Gastric Mucosal Injury through Regulation of Mucin, Acid Secretion, and Inflammatory Pathways.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Petasites japonicus (PJ) has been historically used in East Asian traditional medicine to alleviate gastrointestinal distress, inflammation, and foodborne toxicities. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its gastroprotective efficacy against acute gastric injury remain uncharacterized. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to optimize the extraction conditions and maximize the active-compound yields from PJ roots and stems, and systematically evaluate its gastroprotective mechanisms against ethanol-induced acute gastric injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Response surface methodology was employed to optimize extraction in terms of chlorogenic acid and fukinolic acid yields. The optimized PJ ethanol extract (PJEE) was evaluated in vitro using human gastric epithelial cells (n = 3) and in vivo using a Sprague-Dawley rat model of acute gastric injury induced by oral HCl/ethanol administration (n = 7 per group). Statistical significance was assessed using one-way ANOVA followed by Duncan's test (p < 0.05). RESULTS: Optimization yielded PJEE containing 14.80 mg/g chlorogenic acid and 60.36 mg/g fukinolic acid. In vitro, PJEE (25-100 μg/mL) significantly improved cell viability, restored MUC5AC suppression, and attenuated the transcriptional upregulation of acid secretion-related genes, including HRH2 and H+/K+-ATPase subunits (ATP4A and ATP4B), in ethanol-treated cells. PJEE pretreatment suppressed ethanol-induced NF-κB activation, MAPK phosphorylation, and inflammatory molecule expression (p < 0.05). In the HCl/ethanol-induced gastric injury rat model, oral administration of PJEE (50 and 100 mg/kg) significantly reduced gastric ulcer areas (up to 82%, p < 0.01), improved histopathological scores, and decreased NO and TNF-α levels. Restoration of MUC5AC and regulation of inflammatory and acid secretory markers in gastric tissue further supported the in vivo efficacy of PJEE. CONCLUSION: PJEE may mitigate acute gastric mucosal injury by enhancing mucosal defense, regulating the acid-secretory system, and suppressing NF-κB/MAPK-mediated inflammatory pathways, supporting its potential as a natural gastroprotective agent.

articles.title: Rhodiola rosea extract modulates mitochondrial function and enhances stress resilience in vitro and in vivo.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhodiola rosea L. has long been used as traditional medicine for its adaptogenic and metabolic benefits enhancing physical and mental performance, however the cellular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. We investigated Rhodiola rosea extract (RRE) metabolic effect using in vitro models comprising human dermal fibroblasts and hepatoma cells, as well as a Drosophila melanogaster high-sucrose diet (HSD) model. MATERIAL AND METHODS: RRE was characterized by NMR and mass spectrometry. Glucose consumption, Seahorse and bioenergetic analyses were performed in RRE-treated cells. RRE activities toward electron transport chain enzymes were performed in isolated mitochondria. Mitophagy activation was studied using the mt-Keima biosensor and confirmed by Western blot analysis. Locomotor activity and fat bodies imaging were performed in RRE treated flies. RESULTS: RRE treatment activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), enhanced glucose uptake independently of insulin receptor signaling pathway, and shifted metabolism toward glycolysis by mildly inhibiting mitochondrial electron transport chain complexes I and II and ATP synthase. This mild mitochondrial challenge induced mitohormesis, a process in which transient bioenergetic stress triggers compensatory protective responses, enhancing cellular resilience. Consistently, RRE activated PINK1-Parkin-mediated mitophagy and increased cellular resistance to rotenone induced mitochondrial insult. Additionally, RRE exhibited antioxidant and anti-ferroptotic activities. In vivo, RRE supplementation improved locomotor performance and reduced lipid droplet size in flies exposed to HSD-induced metabolic stress. CONCLUSIONS: RRE promotes metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial quality control, enhancing cellular and organismal resilience to metabolic challenges. Our data provide novel mechanistic insights into the effects of RRE supplementation.

articles.title: Tschimganine and isobornyl acrylate induce cell death via Nat2, a FAM210A/B-like protein, in fission yeast.
articles.abstract: Tschimganine (TMN), a monoterpene benzoate extracted from the roots of Ferula species, exhibits insecticidal, fungicidal, and antitumor activities. Isobornyl acrylate (IBOA), a compound widely used in continuous glucose monitoring devices and wearable electronics, has emerged as a major contact allergen. In Schizosaccharomyces pombe, TMN inhibits cell growth, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. Herein, we examined the mechanism by screening an S. pombe nonessential haploid deletion collection for TMN-resistant mutants, revealing that Nat2, a homolog of human FAM210A/B, is required for TMN-induced growth inhibition. Flow cytometry-based viability assays indicated that TMN treatment (14 μg/mL, 46 μM) and Nat2 overexpression induced cell death. Furthermore, TMN induced nat2+ expression, affected the subcellular localization of Nat2, and induced Nat2-dependent mitochondrial morphological changes. We also observed differences in the expression of multiple genes between WT and Δnat2 cells following TMN treatment. Microscopic observations revealed that TMN-induced cell death was accompanied by apoptosis-like features, including phosphatidylserine exposure on the cell surface and nuclear fragmentation, and that Nat2 influenced both phenotypes. We further demonstrated that IBOA (90 μg/mL, 430 μM) also induces Nat2-dependent cell death in S. pombe, indicating that Nat2-dependent cytotoxicity extends beyond TMN to a structurally related compound of clinical relevance. Interestingly, no identifiable FAM210A/B-like proteins were detected in Ferula in our database analysis, raising the possibility that the lack of these proteins contributes to self-protection against TMN, although this hypothesis remains untested.

articles.title: Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Elevated plasma S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) levels increase the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Since lipophagy maintains cholesterol homeostasis through hydrolysis of cholesterol esters to support efflux, its impairment reduces cholesterol efflux. We aimed to explore the association of elevated SAH with macrophage foam-cell cholesterol handling and the potential mechanisms involving autophagy-related lipid processing and cholesterol efflux. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We explored the associations between plasma SAH levels and cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) in the Guangdong Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) Cohort. Adenosine dialdehyde (AdOx) was used to increase intracellular SAH levels in THP-1 macrophage foam cells, followed by evaluation of cholesterol efflux and autophagy-related lipid handling. We investigated the molecular mechanisms by examining regulators, including ABCA1, vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) subunits, and transcription factor EB (TFEB). Torin 1 was used to assess changes in TFEB-related signaling and cholesterol efflux. KEY FINDINGS: We found that plasma SAH levels were inversely associated with CEC in CAD patients. In vitro, AdOx treatment increased intracellular SAH and reduced ABCA1 expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. AdOx treatment was accompanied by reduced TFEB nuclear translocation, lower ATP6V1H and lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) expression, altered LC3/p62 levels, and increased lysosomal cholesterol. Torin 1 partially restored TFEB-related gene expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. These findings support the involvement of TFEB-V-ATPase-related lysosomal signaling in AdOx-associated changes in macrophage cholesterol handling. SIGNIFICANCE: Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling, identifying SAH metabolism and TFEB-V-ATPase signaling as potential targets for further investigation.

articles.title: Gestational Zika virus infection causes oxidative distress in both mouse and human placentae.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection causes Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS) and has a greater tropism for the placenta. Placental oxidative distress is largely related to pregnancy complications. However, there is no information about how placental oxidative distress contributes to the development of CZS. Here, we hypothesized that ZIKV causes placental oxidative distress. MATERIALS AND METHODS: C57BL/6 pregnant dams were infected at gestational day (GD)12.5. Placentae and fetuses were harvested and separated by sex at GD18.5. Human placentae from ZIKV-pregnant women were also analyzed. Immunohistochemistry, 2D OxyBlot, transmission electron microscopy, qPCR, reduced thiol content, and antioxidant enzymes activities were performed. KEY FINDINGS: ZIKV reduced placental weight in both sexes. However, we detected increased placental efficiencies associated with normal fetal weight at term. Interestingly, we found that ZIKV increased the brain weight of female fetuses. ZIKV increased protein carbonyls and nitrotyrosine residues in the female and male placentae. Mitochondria degeneration and dilated rough endoplasmic reticulum cisternae were found in ZIKV-infected placentae of both sexes. Oxidant (Nox1 and Cybb) and antioxidant (Sod2, Sod3, Gpx1, and Gpx3) genes were upregulated in the female placentae, while only Gpx3 was upregulated by ZIKV in the male placentae. Reduced thiol levels, SOD, GPx, and CAT activities were not changed in both placental sexes. In the human placentae, ZIKV increased nitrotyrosine residues and did not change NOX expression. SIGNIFICANCE: Gestational ZIKV infection causes oxidative distress in both mouse and human placentae. This alteration can be related to placental growth restriction and likely contribute to the development of CZS.

articles.title: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in amniotic fluid-derived cells.
articles.abstract: AIM: Foetal sex is increasingly recognized as a critical biological variable influencing immune development and susceptibility to intrauterine stressors, including infection. However, the mechanisms by which foetal sex modulates innate immune responses at the maternal-foetal interface remain poorly understood. METHODS: We investigated sex-dependent innate immune responses in human amniotic fluid-derived cells (AFCs) using an in vitro model of infection with two pre-term birth-related pathogens, Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS) and Escherichia coli. We evaluated gene and protein expression of key pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α), Toll-like receptors (TLR2 and TLR4), and selected microRNAs (miRNAs), involved both in pro-inflammatory signalling pathways and negative regulators of inflammation. KEY FINDINGS: GBS infection induced a selective inflammatory response characterized by increased TNF-α production and TLR2 protein expression, with stronger responses observed in male AFCs. In contrast, female AFCs exhibited enhanced expression of regulatory miRNAs, including miR-29 family members, associated with reduced TNF-α levels. E. coli infection had a limited functional impact on the inflammatory parameters in our experimental conditions. Although it induced transcriptional activation of inflammatory genes, no significant changes were observed at the protein level. In female cells, E. coli infection was associated with increased expression of miR-146a-5p and miR-19a-3p, along with a reduction in miR-18a-5p. SIGNIFICANCE: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in AFCs. This sex-dependent immune modulation may contribute to differential susceptibility to inflammation-driven pregnancy complications and highlights the importance of incorporating foetal sex as a biological variable in studies of intrauterine infection.

articles.title: Combined polymeric and mesoporous carriers for hot-melt extruded resveratrol amorphous solid dispersions: processability, amorphization, and storage stability.
articles.abstract: Resveratrol (RSV) has poor aqueous solubility and a strong tendency to recrystallize, limiting the performance of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs). This study investigated whether combining polymeric and mesoporous carriers could enable hot-melt extrusion (HME) of physically stable RSV ASDs and how polymer composition, carrier type and content, and RSV loading influenced processability, initial amorphization, and storage stability. Formulations containing PEG 6000, HPMC AS, or Eudragit® EPO, with Syloid® 244 FP or Neusilin® US2, were prepared at RSV loadings of 20-40% (w/w) relative to total polymer mass. Polymers were used either alone or in combination with PEG in ratios 2:1, 1:1, or 1:2. Processable formulations were characterized for RSV content and physical state and re-evaluated after three months under accelerated storage conditions. Mesoporous carriers reduced RSV crystallinity compared to carrier-free PEG systems, while PEG improved extrusion performance. RSV loading was the strongest determinant of crystallinity, with higher loadings producing greater detectable crystallinity after extrusion and after accelerated storage, whereas the formulations showing the g+reatest physical stability contained 20% RSV. Polymer type and polymer-to-PEG ratio showed no significant overall effect on crystallinity after storage. Notably, Neusilin® often promoted superior initial amorphization, yet Neusilin®-containing formulations showed higher crystallinity than corresponding Syloid® formulations after storage. Thus, conditions favoring amorphization during HME do not necessarily provide the greatest resistance to recrystallization, highlighting the need to optimize processability and long-term physical stability separately.

articles.title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE for Targeted Alpha Therapy of Neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: High-risk neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of pediatric cancer mortality. Radioligand therapy targeting somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) with the β-emitter [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE) is under clinical investigation. Alpha-emitters such as actinium-225 (²²⁵Ac) cause more potent, localized DNA damage owing to higher linear energy transfer and shorter path length. We aimed to establish a robust labeling protocol for [²²⁵Ac]Ac-DOTATATE (²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE) for preclinical use and to compare its in vitro cytotoxicity with ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE in neuroblastoma cell lines. METHODS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was synthesized using 5 µg DOTATATE per MBq ²²⁵Ac, and ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE at 60 MBq/nmol in 25 mM sodium ascorbate/50 mM sodium acetate (pH 5). SSTR2-mediated binding of ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE to IMR-32, SK-N-AS and BON cells was measured in real time (LigandTracer). Cytotoxicity was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® viability assay and DNA double-strand breaks by γH2AX immunofluorescence. RESULTS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was obtained with >95% radiochemical purity and remained stable for at least 48 h. ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE bound specifically to SSTR2-positive IMR-32 cells, with low binding to SSTR2-low BON and minimal binding to SSTR2-negative SK-N-AS cells. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) was 0.0049 kBq/mL for ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE and 5.4 kBq/mL for ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE, an approximately 1000-fold lower activity concentration required for alpha as compared with beta emitter. γH2AX analysis indicated a trend toward greater DNA damage with ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE. These findings support further development of SSTR2-targeted alpha therapy for high-risk neuroblastoma.

articles.title: Intramuscular administration of the long-acting cocaine hydrolase CocH5-Fc(M6) protects against cocaine-induced toxicity in male and female mice.
articles.abstract: Acute cocaine intoxication remains a major medical emergency, yet no US Food and Drug Administration-approved medication directly eliminates cocaine or reverses its toxicity. We previously demonstrated that intravenous administration of the engineered cocaine hydrolase CocH5-Fc(M6) effectively protects rodents against cocaine-induced toxicity. Here, we evaluated whether intramuscular administration, a more clinically practical route, provides comparable protection. Male and female CD-1 mice received intramuscular CocH5-Fc(M6) (1, 3, or 10 mg/kg) ∼10 minutes before intraperitoneal administration of a lethal dose of cocaine (100 mg/kg). Surviving mice were rechallenged 24 hours later with 180 mg/kg cocaine (a lethal dose 100% [LD100] dose). Cocaine-induced convulsions, lethality, locomotor activity, and plasma concentrations of active CocH5-Fc(M6) were evaluated. Intramuscular administration of 10 mg/kg CocH5-Fc(M6) completely prevented cocaine-induced convulsions and lethality in both sexes and fully protected all animals against the second cocaine challenge. Intramuscular administration of 3 mg/kg also provided complete protection in male mice in both challenges, whereas 1 mg/kg markedly attenuated cocaine toxicity, completely prevented lethality following the initial cocaine challenge but did not fully prevent convulsions or lethality after the second challenge at 24 hours. CocH5-Fc(M6) dose-dependently attenuated cocaine-induced locomotor hyperactivity, and the time course of protection was consistent with the pharmacokinetic profile of the intramuscularly administered enzyme. These findings demonstrate that intramuscular administration of CocH5-Fc(M6) provides rapid, dose-dependent, and sustained protection against both behavioral and lethal manifestations of acute cocaine toxicity, supporting its further development as a practical enzyme-based therapy for cocaine intoxication. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Acute cocaine intoxication lacks an approved pharmacological treatment that directly eliminates cocaine. This study demonstrates that intramuscular administration of the engineered cocaine hydrolase CocH5-Fc(M6) rapidly, dose-dependently, and durably protects mice against cocaine-induced convulsions, lethality, and locomotor stimulation, with protection lasting at least 24 hours. These findings establish intramuscular delivery as a clinically practical route for enzyme therapy and support further development of CocH5-Fc(M6) as a treatment for acute cocaine intoxication.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel imidazolium-based derivatives as cholinesterase inhibitors: kinetic, molecular docking, and ADMET studies.
articles.abstract: In this study, novel imidazolium-based derivatives (1a-1 l) that are cholinesterase inhibitors were synthesized as potential therapeutic agents for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Their structures were elucidated using 13C-NMR and 1 H-NMR techniques. The inhibitory effects on acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) of the derivatives were examined in vitro and in silico. Most of the synthesized derivatives exhibited higher inhibitory activity than the reference compound, with IC50 values ranging from 21.93 to 50.58 nM for AChE and from 78.75 to 133.27 nM for BChE. The corresponding KI values ranged from 3.72 ± 0.06 to 8.60 ± 0.57 nM for AChE and from 34.58 ± 0.36 to 250.68 ± 72.95 nM for BChE. Molecular docking analysis revealed that compound 1e displayed the highest docking score against BChE (- 8.933 kcal/mol), and compound 1a showed the highest Glide docking score toward AChE (- 12.151 kcal/mol). The in silico ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) profiles of two newly synthesized imidazolium-based compounds (1a and 1i) were evaluated and compared against tacrine, a well-known cholinesterase inhibitor used as a reference standard. The analysis reveals that both novel compounds demonstrate higher hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity profiles compared to tacrine, with compounds 1a additionally showing potentially favorable blood-brain barrier penetration, metabolic stability, and lower mutagenicity risk. These findings indicate that the derivatives may represent potential structural candidates for further investigation as cholinesterase inhibitors relevant to AD. Further studies involving comprehensive pharmacokinetic, in vivo efficacy, and toxicity evaluations are warranted to validate the therapeutic potential of these imidazolium-based derivatives as cholinesterase inhibitors.

articles.title: Nefopam as a neuroprotective agent in Alzheimer's disease: network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a progressive neurodegenerative disorder marked by declining cognition, deteriorating memory, and behavioural abnormalities, with no disease-modifying therapy established despite decades of investigation. This study investigated whether nefopam - a non-opioid, centrally acting analgesic - could be repositioned as a neuroprotective agent against AD. An integrated strategy was adopted, combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and an in vivo assessment using a scopolamine-induced rat model. Eight crystal structures representing seven AD-relevant targets were selected for the computational work: MAOB (1GOS), OPRM1 (4DKL), GRIN1 (4KFQ), SLC6A3 (4M48), HTR2A (6A93 and 8ZMG), SLC6A4 (7LWD), and the GluN1/GluN2B NMDA receptor (3QEL). Docking was performed with Glide, binding free energies were estimated by MM-GBSA, and complexes were simulated for 100 ns with Desmond. Network pharmacology analysis revealed 90 shared targets between nefopam and AD-associated pathways, pointing toward a multi-target mode of action. Docking followed by MM-GBSA calculations indicated favourable binding of nefopam across the selected targets, with the most favourable MM-GBSA ΔG bind values observed for HTR2A (6A93; - 65.77 kcal/mol), GRIN1 (- 58.28 kcal/mol), HTR2A (8ZMG; - 58.13 kcal/mol), and SLC6A4 (- 57.65 kcal/mol). Subsequent MD simulations indicated stable binding behaviour for SLC6A3 (4M48), HTR2A (6A93), and SLC6A4 (7LWD); GRIN1 (4KFQ) and MAOB (1GOS) displayed moderate stability, whereas HTR2A (8ZMG) showed instability at the protein level despite the ligand remaining reasonably well retained. In the in vivo phase, nefopam produced a dose-dependent improvement in neurobehavioural outcomes across the different assessment points. Biochemical analysis further showed a marked decline in MDA levels together with a significant rise in SOD and CAT activity, reflecting a meaningful antioxidant response. These findings suggest that nefopam exerts neuroprotective, antioxidant, and cognition-improving effects in the scopolamine-induced model of cognitive impairment, possibly involving serotonergic, glutamatergic, and monoaminergic signalling routes. Additional in vitro, mechanistic, and clinical research is needed before its repurposing for AD can be therapeutically confirmed.

articles.title: Sinomenine attenuates neuroinflammation and neurological deficits following intracerebral hemorrhage: involvement of CaMKIIα-AKT and cAMP-PKA-CREB signaling.
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating subtype of stroke characterized by high acute mortality and persistent neurological impairment, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain lacking. Sinomenine, a bioactive alkaloid derived from Sinomenium acutum, has shown neuroprotective efficacy across diverse neurological disorders; however, its role in ICH remains insufficiently characterized. To investigate the therapeutic potential and mechanisms of sinomenine against ICH, a combined approach integrating network-based pharmacology, in silico docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and in vivo experiments was employed in this study. Network analysis identified AKT1, EGFR, GSK3B, MMP9, and mTOR as central candidate targets, while GO and KEGG enrichment analyses identified the PI3K-Akt, cAMP, and NF-κB pathways as potentially key players. In silico docking and subsequent MD simulations revealed stable interaction of sinomenine with AKT1, EGFR, GSK3B, and mTOR. Consistent with these in silico predictions, sinomenine administration significantly ameliorated neurological impairment and attenuated brain edema in a rat model of ICH. Further mechanistic investigations revealed that sinomenine may modulate cAMP-PKA-CREB signaling and the CaMKIIα-AKT axis, accompanied by reduced NF-κB expression, downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and upregulation of BDNF. Together, these findings suggest that the protective effects of sinomenine against experimental ICH may involve coordinated changes in inflammatory and neurotrophic signaling pathways. This study provides experimental data supporting sinomenine as a promising multi-target therapeutic agent against ICH.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and genetic association analyses prioritize FASN as a potential molecular link between cigarette smoke exposure and male infertility.
articles.abstract: Male infertility (MIF) is a complex reproductive disorder influenced by genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors. Cigarette smoke (CS) contains numerous reproductive toxicants and has been associated with impaired semen quality and fertility. However, the molecular mechanisms linking CS exposure to MIF remain unclear. Representative toxic constituents of CS were selected based on previous studies, and multiple databases were integrated to identify CS associated targets, which were intersected with MIF associated genes to obtain CS-MIF common targets. Three MIF transcriptomic datasets (GSE6872, GSE34514, and GSE22331) were integrated for differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Candidate genes were identified by integrating CS-MIF targets, differentially expressed genes, and WGCNA-derived key module genes, followed by LASSO and SVM-RFE machine learning analyses. Associations between genetically predicted candidate gene expression and MIF risk were investigated using cis-eQTL-based two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) analysis using testis-derived eQTL data was subsequently performed to provide complementary tissue-specific genetic evidence for FASN. Molecular docking suggested potential structural compatibility between FASN and several representative CS-associated compounds, while MD simulation supported the structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex. Finally, TM4 Sertoli cells were exposed to cigarette smoke condensate (CSC), and FASN mRNA expression was evaluated by RT-qPCR. Four hub genes, including ABCC1, FASN, GAPDH, and SGK1, were identified from 14 candidate genes. MR analysis demonstrated that genetically predicted higher FASN expression was significantly associated with increased MIF risk (IVW: OR = 1.256, 95% CI = 1.109-1.423, P < 0.001; FDR-adjusted P = 0.004). SMR analysis using testis eQTL data further supported the association between FASN expression and MIF (P_SMR = 0.040, P_HEIDI = 0.307). Molecular docking identified benzanthrone as the compound with the most favorable predicted binding affinity for FASN among the 20 selected compounds (- 7.129 kcal/mol). Subsequent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation suggested structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex under the investigated conditions. Furthermore, exposure of TM4 Sertoli cells to 100 μg/mL CSC for 24 h significantly increased FASN mRNA expression. This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, machine learning, genetic association analyses, structural simulations, and in vitro experiments to prioritize FASN as a candidate gene potentially relevant to CS-associated male reproductive dysfunction. Genetically predicted higher FASN expression was associated with increased MIF risk, while CSC exposure increased FASN mRNA expression in TM4 Sertoli cells. However, these findings do not establish that FASN mediates CS-induced reproductive injury. Further functional investigations are required to clarify its potential mechanistic role.

articles.title: Bergenin ameliorates anxiety- and depression-like behavior in antibiotic-treated mice: behavioral and in silico insights.
articles.abstract: Broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure perturbs the gut microbiota and has been linked to anxiety- and depression-like behavior in rodents. Bergenin, an anti-inflammatory, antioxidant isocoumarin C-glycoside, has not previously been evaluated in this setting. Swiss albino mice received a 14-day oral-gavage antibiotic regimen (ampicillin, neomycin, metronidazole ≈10 mg/kg/day each; vancomycin ≈5 mg/kg/day), followed by 14 days of oral bergenin (25 or 50 mg/kg/day) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg/day, reference). Anxiety-like behavior was assessed by the elevated plus maze and open field test, and depression-like behavior by the forced swim and tail suspension tests. Docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics characterized bergenin's predicted binding to TLR4-MD-2 and the serotonin transporter (SERT), and ADMET/toxicity profiles were predicted. Antibiotic treatment produced weight loss and anxiety- and depression-like phenotypes across all four assays. Bergenin dose-dependently attenuated these deficits (high dose = ≈70-92% recovery) without altering behavior or body weight in antibiotic-free animals. Bergenin was predicted to occupy the SERT S1 site (ΔG =  - 7.9 kcal/mol) with simulated stability resembling fluoxetine, whereas its TLR4-MD-2 interaction (ΔG =  - 5.4 kcal/mol) was shallow and hydrogen bond poor relative to Eritoran. Its predicted ADMET profile was Lipinski-compliant, with some unverified toxicity alerts. Limitations include antibiotic doses lower than published protocols and no microbiome, biochemical, or molecular assays; dysbiosis, microbial recovery, and mechanism were not verified. Effects are interpreted in antibiotic-treated mice, and in silico findings are hypothesis-generating. Bergenin ameliorated anxiety- and depression-like behavior in antibiotic-treated mice; in silico data favored serotonergic over direct TLR4-MD-2 involvement, warranting experimental validation.

articles.title: Levothyroxine administration timing during Ramadan: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Levothyroxine (LT4) must be taken on an empty stomach, a requirement difficult to reconcile with the compressed nocturnal eating window of Ramadan. Three dosing times are commonly used, at sunset before the iftar meal (preiftar), at least 3 h after iftar (postiftar) and before the predawn suhoor meal (presuhoor), and a predawn schedule independent of the last meal has recently been tested. Their comparative effects have not been assessed in a synthesis restricted to randomized evidence. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing two or more LT4 dosing times during Ramadan in adults with primary hypothyroidism or prior total thyroidectomy were eligible. The primary outcome was the change in thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) from before to after Ramadan. Mean differences (MDs) in mIU/l were pooled with a random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals) when at least two trials reporting arm-level means and standard deviations shared a comparison; other evidence was synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE (PROSPERO CRD420261482621). Five RCTs (712 participants analysed) were included. Two trials reported TSH only as model-based percentiles or box plots and were synthesized narratively or in sensitivity analyses; the preiftar-versus-predawn comparison (one trial) was also synthesized narratively. For preiftar versus presuhoor dosing (2 RCTs, n = 149), the MD in TSH change was - 0.61 mIU/l (95% CI - 6.67 to 5.45; common-effect 95% CI - 1.94 to 0.71) and that in post-Ramadan TSH was - 0.24 mIU/l (common-effect 95% CI - 1.72 to 1.23). Single trials compared preiftar with postiftar dosing (MD 0.10 mIU/l; 95% CI - 1.62 to 1.82; n = 65), postiftar with presuhoor dosing (MD - 2.10; 95% CI - 6.14 to 1.94; n = 56) and preiftar with predawn dosing (MD - 0.33; 95% CI - 1.14 to 0.48; n = 302). Estimates were similar across assumed pre-post correlations of 0.2 to 0.8 and after adding converted data from a further trial. Two trials were at high overall risk of bias, and certainty of evidence was low to very low for all comparisons. Randomized evidence does not show that any single levothyroxine dosing time during Ramadan is superior. However, confidence intervals were wide and compatible with clinically important differences in either direction, so the regimens cannot be considered equivalent. Adherence differed between regimens in individual trials, but its importance relative to timing was not established. Adequately powered trials with objective adherence measurement are needed.

articles.title: Alisol B attenuates rotenone-induced oxidative injury in SH-SY5Y cells: AKT-associated protection and changes in p38 MAPK phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: Alisol B is a protostane-type triterpenoid whose protective effects against rotenone-induced neuronal cell injury remain unclear. This study investigates Alisol B pretreatment against acute rotenone-induced injury in SH-SY5Y cells and associated AKT and p38 MAPK signaling changes. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and three independent 300-ns molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify candidate targets and explore predicted protein-ligand interactions. SH-SY5Y cells were pretreated with Alisol B before acute rotenone exposure. Cellular metabolic activity was assessed by CCK-8, ROS-associated fluorescence by DCFH-DA, apoptosis by Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry, and AKT and p38 MAPK phosphorylation by Western blotting. MK-2206 was used to investigate the functional involvement of AKT-associated signaling. A total of 397 overlapping candidate targets were identified, and AKT1 showed the highest degree in the protein-protein interaction network. Docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported the structural plausibility of a predicted Alisol B-AKT1 interaction but did not establish direct target engagement. Alisol B pretreatment partially improved cellular metabolic activity, reduced ROS-associated fluorescence, and decreased apoptosis after rotenone exposure. MK-2206 attenuated the effects of Alisol B on cellular metabolic activity and ROS-associated fluorescence. Alisol B was also associated with increased AKT phosphorylation and decreased p38 MAPK phosphorylation. Alisol B pretreatment provided preliminary protection against acute rotenone-induced injury in SH-SY5Y cells.

articles.title: TRPV1 signaling mediates remote ischemic preconditioning-induced neuroprotection in a mouse model of bilateral common carotid artery occlusion/reperfusion-induced vascular dementia.
articles.abstract: Vascular dementia (VD) is a leading cause of cognitive impairment associated with cerebrovascular pathology. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a non-invasive strategy that induces endogenous neuroprotection against ischemic insults; however, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The present study investigated the involvement of transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) in RIPC-mediated neuroprotection against bilateral common carotid artery occlusion/reperfusion (BCCAo/R)-induced vascular-related cerebral ischemic injury with early cognitive dysfunction. RIPC was applied prior to ischemia using three cycles of 5 min ischemia followed by 5 min reperfusion. TRPV1 and mechanosensitive ion channels were pharmacologically modulated using capsaicin, gadolinium, ruthenium red, and capsazepine. Behavioral, biochemical, histopathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular parameters were evaluated. BCCAo/R-induced mice exhibited significant impairments in locomotor activity, motor coordination, neurological function, spatial learning, and memory, accompanied by increased cerebral infarction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, neuronal injury, apoptosis, reactive gliosis, and NF-κB gene expression. RIPC and capsaicin improved behavioral performance, reduced infarct volume, restored antioxidant defenses, normalized acetylcholinesterase activity, and attenuated oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, neuronal injury, and NF-κB expression. Both interventions restored the Bcl-2/caspase - 3 balance, preserved neuronal morphology, increased TRPV1 immunoreactivity, and reduced Iba-1 and GFAP activation. Importantly, RIPC-mediated neuroprotection was attenuated by gadolinium, ruthenium red, and capsazepine, supporting involvement of mechanosensitive and TRP-channel signaling, particularly TRPV1. Collectively, these findings provide preliminary pharmacological evidence that TRPV1-associated signaling contributes to RIPC-mediated neuroprotection, potentially through modulation of NF-κB-associated inflammatory responses.

articles.title: In silico analysis toward functional genomic profiling and bioprospecting Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines. METHODS: This study focused on isolating bacteria from different kinds of soil and contaminated coconut samples. The protease-positive isolates were screened for anti-inflammatory potential using the human red blood cell (HRBC) membrane stabilization assay and the inhibition of protein denaturation by an egg albumin method. Whole-genome sequencing was carried out for most promising isolate followed by in silico genomic analysis using antiSMASH, deepBGC, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), KofamScan, and eggNOG-mapper automatic annotation servers. RESULT: The current work targets the anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential of an isolated bacterial strain VITVS26, which was taxonomically identified as Serratia rubidaea through whole-genome sequencing with a genome size of 5.29 Mb and a GC content of 58.56%. Protease-producing S. rubidaea VITVS26 has exhibited a maximum of 90.5% ± 0.4% of human red blood cell stabilization and 83.33% ± 0.152% of protein denaturation inhibiting capacity during the egg albumin method. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) confirmed the presence of a putative anti-inflammatory protease in VITVS26. In addition, the isolate has shown 52.62% ± 1.158% free radical scavenging capacity at 1,000 μg/mL concentration with an IC50 value of 632 μg/mL. Upon the purification of the anti-inflammatory protease, specific activity was increased from 15,461.18 to 25,182.86 with a purification fold of 1.63 and a recovery of 12.26%. The draft genome profiling of S. rubidaea VITVS26 revealed a total of 4,883 genes with 68.8% functional assignment, and in silico analysis predicted 41 host-immunomodulatory genes, 49 antioxidant genes, and 15 biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) regions. The pigmentation of VITVS26 is supported by the secondary metabolite prodigiosin and its associated genes with a possible role in the bioactivity of the isolate. Bioinformatic screening confirmed the complete absence of horizontally acquired antimicrobial resistance genes in strain VITVS26. CONCLUSION: An overall strong positive anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity was exhibited by S. rubidaea VITVS26 supported by bioactive, functional, and genomic evidence. The presence of prodigiosin and aryl polyene provides better scope in the future for utilization of S. rubidaea VITVS26 in biotechnology industries after safety evaluation.

articles.title: Medicarpin suppresses gastric cancer growth in association with inhibition of mevalonate pathway-associated cholesterol biosynthesis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gastric cancer (GC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by metabolic reprogramming, including dysregulated cholesterol biosynthesis. Medicarpin (Med), a natural isoflavan isolated from Radix Hedysari, has shown pharmacological potential. However, its anti-GC activity and underlying metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The effects of Med on AGS and HGC-27 cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, and migration were evaluated. Antitumor activity and tolerability were evaluated in a nude mouse xenograft model. Integrated untargeted metabolomics and quantitative proteomics identified Med-associated metabolic alterations and potential targets. Western blotting, cholesterol quantification, filipin staining, and exogenous cholesterol rescue assays were performed to further investigate the proposed mechanism. RESULTS: Med significantly inhibited AGS and HGC-27 cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, and migration in a concentration- and time-dependent manner, with minimal cytotoxicity toward normal gastric mucosal GES-1 cells. In xenografts, Med reduced tumor volume and weight without significant body weight loss or histopathological injury in major organs. Multi-omics analyses revealed extensive metabolic remodeling, with marked suppression of lipid, steroid, and primary bile acid biosynthesis. Proteomics and Western blotting showed that Med downregulated key enzymes in the mevalonate pathway, including mevalonate kinase (MVK), 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 1 (HMGCS1), and lanosterol synthase (LSS), accompanied by reduced intracellular cholesterol levels. Exogenous cholesterol supplementation partially reversed Med-induced inhibition of GC cell viability, proliferation, and colony formation. CONCLUSION: Med inhibits GC growth in association with the downregulation of MVK, HMGCS1, and LSS and the inhibition of mevalonate pathway-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis. These findings suggest that Med may represent a potential natural compound for targeting lipid metabolic reprogramming in GC.

articles.title: Mechanism of Glycyrrhiza and glycyrrhetinic acid in cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury: a proteomics and metabolomics study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication associated with cisplatin (CP), severely limiting its clinical use. Glycyrrhiza (GL) has been clinically used in China for detoxification, and its primary active ingredient, Glycyrrhetinic acid (GA), demonstrates detoxification effects. Studies conducted previously have shown that GL and GA offer protection against CP-induced AKI. However, the precise mechanism underlying this effect is unclear. PURPOSE: The mechanisms of GL and GA in alleviating CP-induced AKI were investigated using proteomics and metabolomics. METHODS: A rat model of CP-induced AKI was established. Proteomics using DDA-PASEF-based label-free LC-MS/MS and metabolomics using UPLC-Q-TOF MS were employed to detect differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and metabolites (DEMs) in renal tissues and plasma. A protein-protein interaction network between disease targets and DEPs was constructed, correlation analysis and pathway enrichment were employed to uncover the protective mechanisms. To confirm the mechanisms, the primary proteins involved in the above processes were identified using Western blot, immunohistochemistry, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. RESULTS: The interventions alleviated CP-induced AKI, reduced serum BUN and Cr levels and alleviated histopathological renal injury. Proteomics results indicated the participation of GL and GA in biological processes such as complement activation, acute-phase response and inflammatory response by regulating related DEPs. Metabolomics results suggested that DEMs related to lipid, energy, and amino acid metabolism were regulated to alleviate metabolic disorders in kidney injury. GL participated in the multiple pathways related to inflammatory response and apoptosis, and showed an interplay with Agt, Stat2, Vtn, Plg, Cyp2e1, C7, Cfd, and Serping1. GA was found to participate in above pathways via the regulation of DEPs strongly correlated with AKI effector molecules and exhibited a strong interplay with Hspb1, Crp, Cfh, Slc12a1, Vtn, Kng1, and Cdc37. The intervention led to a reversal in the expression of primary proteins involved in these processes, consistent with proteomics findings. CONCLUSION: GL and GA mitigate cisplatin-induced kidney damage through various mechanisms, including the coordinated changes in inflammatory and acute-phase responses, survival/apoptosis-related proteins, and energy, lipid, and amino acid metabolism. These findings identify several candidate molecular networks associated with the renoprotective effects of GL and GA and provide a basis for further mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies genetic markers for taxane-induced multi-organ adverse effects in breast cancer patients.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Taxanes are standard chemotherapeutic agents for breast cancer, yet their clinical utility is often limited by severe multi-organ adverse drug reactions (ADRs), which show marked inter-individual variability. METHODS: To investigate the genetic basis of this variability, we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) in 203 breast cancer patients receiving taxane-based chemotherapy and assessed five ADR phenotypes-neutropenia, leukopenia, rash, peripheral neurotoxicity, and gastrointestinal toxicity. Common variants were tested via single-variant association tests, and rare variants via gene-based burden tests (SKAT-O). RESULTS: In common-variant analysis, PTGES rs2302821 showed a significant association with neutropenia (joint genotype test P = 5.57 × 10-6; adjusted P = 2.19 × 10-6), with the AC genotype conferring a protective effect (adjusted OR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.08-0.35). For rash, rare-variant gene-based analysis nominated GSDMA as a candidate (P = 2.88 × 10-7). GSDMA exhibited skin-specific expression, and missense variants were exclusively observed in affected cases; however, these results remain exploratory given the limited number of rash cases (n = 12). A common-variant signal in IL36B was nominally significant in unadjusted analysis but attenuated after covariate adjustment, warranting further validation. DISCUSSION: Our findings identify PTGES rs2302821 as a potential genetic marker for taxane-induced neutropenia and nominate GSDMA as a preliminary candidate for rash susceptibility, providing a genomic perspective on inter-individual variability in taxane-related ADRs.

articles.title: Neurological adverse events associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a pharmacovigilance study based on the FAERS and JADER databases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurological adverse events (NAEs) have been reported during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but their reporting spectrum and onset patterns across drugs and pharmacovigilance databases remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a pharmacovigilance study of seven ICIs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database. Primary drug-preferred term (PT) signals were evaluated using whole-database disproportionality analyses. An exploratory FAERS analysis compared PD-L1 with PD-1 inhibitors within study-defined tumor-indicator strata. Factors associated with NAE reporting were assessed in FAERS by univariate and multivariable logistic regression, and time-to-onset (TTO) was summarized using descriptive statistics and Weibull analyses. JADER cemiplimab data were summarized descriptively only because of sparse reporting. RESULTS: The analysis included 3,915 NAE reports from FAERS and 2,929 from JADER. The heatmaps displayed 111 positive drug-PT pairs across 31 PTs in FAERS and 49 across 16 PTs in JADER.
