Myasthenia gravis showed a disproportionality signal for all seven ICIs in non-Japanese FAERS reports and for all six ICIs included in the JADER signal analysis; encephalitis-related terms and immune-mediated myositis also recurred, although drug-specific patterns varied. In FAERS, complete-case regression included 111,879 ICI-related reports with 2,887 NAEs. Age ≥65 years and ICI combination therapy were associated with higher adjusted odds of NAE reporting, whereas PD-L1 and CTLA-4 monotherapy were associated with lower adjusted reporting odds relative to PD-1 monotherapy. The stratified comparison showed lower myasthenia gravis reporting odds for PD-L1 than PD-1 in both strata; encephalitis confidence intervals included 1. Drug-level median TTOs ranged from 16 to 43 days in FAERS and from 16 to 32 days in JADER, with heterogeneous Weibull patterns across drugs and databases. CONCLUSION: ICI-associated neurological reports showed recurring neuromuscular and central nervous system signals, partial qualitative concordance between non-Japanese FAERS reports and JADER, and heterogeneous onset patterns across drugs. The observed reporting associations do not establish comparative clinical safety. Overall, these findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in studies with exposure denominators, clinically adjudicated diagnoses, and longitudinal follow-up.

articles.title: Protective effects of Gentiana macrophylla Pall. against blue light-induced retinal injury associated with of antioxidant defense, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of the methanol extract of Gentiana macrophylla Pall. (MEG) against acute blue light (BL)-induced retinal injury and to characterize the associated changes in antioxidant defense, mitochondrial status, apoptosis, and inflammatory responses. METHODS: The phytochemical profile of MEG was characterized using high-performance liquid chromatograph (HPLC), and its chemical radical-scavenging properties were evaluated using cell-free assays. The protective effects of MEG were investigated in A2E/BL-exposed ARPE-19 cells and BL-exposed BALB/c mice following MEG pretreatment. Oxidative stress, mitochondrial membrane potential and morphology, apoptosis- and inflammation-related markers, and retinal histopathological changes were evaluated using biochemical, molecular, imaging, and histological analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen metabolites were tentatively annotated in MEG. MEG pretreatment significantly reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) by 31% and 48% at 100 and 200 μg/mL, respectively, compared with the Vehicle-treated group (p < 0.05). MEG also reduced nitric oxide production and was associated with increased superoxide dismutase expression and Nrf2 phosphorylation in age-related macular degeneration (AMD)-mimicking cells. MEG attenuated mitochondrial structural abnormalities, and was accompanied by changes in mitochondrial biogenesis-related gene expression. Consistently, TMRM fluorescence was increased by 20%-85% following MEG pretreatment (p < 0.05), indicating attenuation of mitochondrial membrane depolarization. In addition, MEG attenuated apoptosis-associated alterations and inflammatory responses involving NF-κB, iNOS, COX-2, and TNF-α. Consistent protective responses were observed in vivo, where MEG pretreatment attenuated BL-induced retinal thinning, increasing whole retinal thickness from 132 ± 4 μm to 187 ± 16 μm at 200 mg/kg (p < 0.05), together with attenuation of associated molecular alterations. Ursolic acid, a selected metabolite detected in MEG, reproduced several cellular responses observed following MEG treatment. CONCLUSION: MEG pretreatment attenuated acute BL-induced retinal injury, accompanied by changes in antioxidant defense-related markers, mitochondrial status, apoptosis-associated alterations, and inflammatory responses. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting further investigation of MEG as a potential protective botanical preparation against oxidative and phototoxic retinal injury.

articles.title: Immunotherapy plus chemotherapy versus immunotherapy alone in esophageal cancer: a real-world pharmacovigilance analysis of safety signals and fatal outcomes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important component of systemic therapy for esophageal cancer, but real-world safety data for combining ICIs with taxane- and platinum-based chemotherapy remain limited. This study compared adverse-event (AE) profiles, time to onset (TTO), and reported mortality between ICI-based combination therapy and ICI monotherapy in esophageal cancer. METHODS: Using the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS), we screened reports from Q3/2019 through Q1/2026 for esophageal cancer involving pembrolizumab or nivolumab as the primary suspect. Combination included immunotherapy with a taxane and platinum; monotherapy included immunotherapy alone. Disproportionality was assessed via reporting odds ratios (RORs) and proportional reporting ratios (PRRs). TTO was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, and logistic regression examined factors for reported mortality. RESULTS: Among 1,580 eligible reports (103 combination, 1,477 monotherapy), distinct AE signal profiles emerged. In combination, prominent signals were gastrointestinal, hematologic, and respiratory, with esophagitis showing the strongest signal (ROR, 61.97; 95%CI, 22.80-168.48), followed by decreased lymphocyte count (ROR, 59.68; 95%CI, 28.99-122.83) and behaviour disorder (ROR, 42.85; 95%CI, 13.58-135.17). In monotherapy, signals were more immune-mediated, including immune-mediated cystitis (ROR, 261.05; 95%CI, 113.92-598.18), immune-mediated cholangitis (ROR, 87.65; 95%CI, 41.36-185.78), immune-mediated endocrinopathy (ROR, 85.51; 95%CI, 27.19-268.89) and so on. Among 571 reports with TTO data, AEs occurred significantly earlier in combination than monotherapy, with median TTOs of 23 days (IQR, 8-72) vs. 49 days (IQR, 21-129) (log-rank P < 0.001), consistent across age, sex, weight, and reporting-year subgroups. Reported mortality was 6.8% for combination vs. 21.1% for monotherapy. After multivariable adjustment, combination was associated with lower reported mortality odds than monotherapy (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95%CI, 0.06-0.77; P = 0.033). CONCLUSION: ICI-based combination therapy showed a distinct AE profile and significantly earlier AE onset than monotherapy, but lower reported mortality odds. These findings underscore the need for early monitoring of hematologic, gastrointestinal, and respiratory toxicities during combination therapy.

articles.title: Surufatinib and camrelizumab plus nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine as first-line treatment for metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Surufatinib targets angiogenic and myeloid signaling pathways that may contribute to resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We evaluated surufatinib and camrelizumab added to nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine (AG) in routine first-line treatment. METHODS: This exploratory single-center retrospective cohort included 132 patients with metastatic PDAC and documented proficient mismatch repair or microsatellite stability who started first-line treatment during 2022-2025. Forty-four received surufatinib-camrelizumab plus AG and 88 received AG. Real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was the primary outcome. Overall survival (OS), tumor response, safety, and treatment delivery were also assessed. Survival associations were adjusted for clinically selected baseline factors. RESULTS: Median rwPFS was 6.3 months with the combination and 4.1 months with AG (log-rank P = 0.021); the adjusted hazard ratio was 0.73 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-1.12; P = 0.152). Median OS was 9.7 versus 8.4 months (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.57-1.38). Unconfirmed objective response rates were 45.5% and 19.3%, respectively (P = 0.004). Confirmed response rates were 38.6% and 15.9% (P = 0.005). CA19-9 declined more in the combination group among patients with eligible paired measurements (P = 0.032). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 47.7% versus 34.1%, and toxicity-related permanent discontinuation occurred in 18.2% versus 11.4%. Median relative dose intensity was 87.0% versus 87.9% for both chemotherapy agents, 79.1% for prescribed surufatinib, and 100.0% for camrelizumab. Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan-Meier estimation was not estimable in either group. CONCLUSION: Surufatinib-camrelizumab plus AG was associated with higher unconfirmed and confirmed response rates, without significant adjusted rwPFS or OS differences. The findings support prospective evaluation with attention to dose optimization and toxicity management.

articles.title: A pectic polysaccharide from Codonopsis pilosula alleviates cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression and intestinal immune dysregulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Codonopsis pilosula is a classic immunomodulatory traditional Chinese medicine. Its polysaccharides exert dual regulatory effects on systemic and intestinal immune responses. Our previous work prepared a pectic polysaccharide from C. pilosula (CPP1b) exhibited significant bioactivity. However, whether CPP1b alleviates cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced immunosuppression and intestinal immune dysregulation remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the immunomodulatory and intestinal protective effects of CPP1b in immunosuppressed mice. METHODS: The regulatory effects of CPP1b on systemic and intestinal immunity were evaluated by multiple indicators including body weight, immune organ indexes, hematological parameters, inflammatory cytokines, pathological changes in the spleen and intestine. 16S rDNA sequencing was employed to analyze the gut microbial composition. Meanwhile, we quantified the dynamic changes of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in feces during the administration period by gas chromatography. The protein expression levels of GPR41, GPR43 and GPR109A were assessed by Western blotting. Finally, correlation heatmap was generated by cluster analysis to explore the associations between the key differential microbiota and physicochemical/immunological parameters. RESULTS: CPP1b significantly ameliorated CTX-induced body weight loss (P < 0.01), increased thymus and spleen indexes (P < 0.01), restored peripheral immune cell counts and CD4+/CD8+ T cell ratios (P < 0.05), increased pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and IFN-γ (P < 0.05). Meanwhile, CPP1b alleviated intestinal mucosal damage and increased intestinal IgA expression, increased the number of colonic goblet cells. CPP1b reshaped the gut microbial community and diversity, with the microbiota composition shifting toward the normal state. Dynamic SCFAs profiling further demonstrated that CPP1b progressively elevated total SCFAs level, with acetate and butyrate showing significant differences (P < 0.05). Western blotting results demonstrated that CPP1b significantly upregulated the protein expression of G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs)-GPR41, GPR43 and GPR109A (P < 0.05). Correlation analysis suggested potential associations between gut microbiota and physiological, metabolic, and immunological changes during CPP1b treatment. CONCLUSION: CPP1b can effectively alleviate CTX-induced immunosuppression and intestinal immune dysregulation by protecting immune organs and modulating humoral, cellular, and intestinal immunity. This study highlights the potential of CPP1b, a pectic polysaccharide from Codonopsis pilosula, as a source of bioactive polysaccharides with immunomodulatory effects.

articles.title: β-glucosidase-mediated hydrolysis of Ophiocordyceps polysaccharides enhances antioxidant and immunomodulatory activities and ameliorates intestinal barrier function to maintain gut homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Polysaccharides derived from Ophiocordyceps (Chinese Cordyceps) exhibit notable bioactivities, yet their high molecular weight may limit their fermentability by the gut microbiota, thereby modulating the production of bioactive metabolites. This study aimed to prepare low-molecular-weight Ophiocordyceps polysaccharides (OPs) through enzymatic modification and to elucidate the associated structural alterations and mechanisms underlying intestinal barrier regulation. Hydrolysis with β-glucosidase yielded the enzymatically modified product OPs-80E. Structural characterization demonstrated that hydrolysis significantly reduced the average molecular weight from 8.64 × 105 Da to 2.99 × 104 Da and altered the monosaccharide composition profile. In vitro assays showed that OPs-80E exhibited greater antioxidant capacity and immunomodulatory activity than native OPs-80, as evidenced by enhanced RAW264.7 cell proliferation, phagocytosis, and cytokine secretion. In a cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppressed mouse model, OPs-80E was more effective than OPs-80 in reversing intestinal histopathological damage, significantly upregulating the expression of tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and Claudin-1), and remodeling the gut microbiota architecture. 16S rRNA gene sequencing analysis indicated that OPs-80E significantly enriched butyrate-producing taxa, such as Lachnospiraceae, while suppressing potential pathogens. Correlation network analysis further revealed that OPs-80E established a symbiotic network centered on the Prevotellaceae Ga6A1 group and Clade Ia, facilitating synergistic "polysaccharide degradation and butyrate production" metabolic cross-feeding to maintain intestinal barrier integrity. Collectively, enzymatic hydrolysis represents an effective strategy for enhancing the bioactivity of Chinese Cordyceps polysaccharides. OPs-80E exerts intestinal protective effects by modulating the "microbiota and barrier" axis, highlighting its broad application prospects in functional foods and pharmaceutical development.

articles.title: Hybrid aerogel-loaded ticagrelor cationic hyalurosomes as a platform for wound healing management; in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo studies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to evaluate the restorative effects of ticagrelor (TIC), a well-known antiplatelet drug, on wound-healing capacity using cationic hyalurosomes loaded into an aerogel. METHODS: The ethanol injection method was used to produce cationic hyalurosomes, which were then optimized using a D-optimal design with the type of surfactant (X1), hyaluronic acid (HA) amount (mg) (X2), and phospholipid (PC) amount (mg) (X3) as independent variables. The impact of these variables on the entrapment efficiency (EE%, Y1), particle size (PS, Y2), and zeta potential (ZP, Y3) was evaluated. RESULTS: In vitro assessments revealed that the spherical optimum formula had an EE% of 73.23% ± 0.27%, a PS of 162.95 ± 0.05 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.471 ± 0.004, and a ZP of 27.76 ± 0.77 mV. The optimum formula was stable for up to 90 days. Ex vivo examination using confocal laser scanning microscopy revealed that the optimum formula, labeled with fluorescein, was well deposited throughout the skin. Differential scanning calorimetry studies showed complete encapsulation of TIC within vesicles. The in vitro release study showed a sustained release profile from the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel compared to TIC suspension, TIC aerogel, and the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes. In vivo assessments concluded better skin deposition of the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel and good healing capacity. Moreover, histopathological assessment confirmed the safety of using the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes aerogel, with no evidence of inflammation. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel facilitates wound healing and is a viable option for wound management.

articles.title: Response Heterogeneity to Gegen Qinlian Decoction in Ameliorating Insulin Sensitivity Is Associated With Osteopontin Expression.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize heterogeneity in the anti-hyperglycaemic response to Gegen Qinlian decoction (GQD) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice and identify response-associated candidate proteins. METHODS: T2DM mice were established by a high-fat diet and streptozotocin. Glycaemic control and response heterogeneity were assessed using blood glucose measurements. Serum insulin concentrations and pancreatic histomorphology were used as surrogate markers of pancreatic β-cell function (BCF). Insulin tolerance testing and an insulin-resistant HepG2 cell model were used to assess insulin sensitivity-related phenotypes. Candidate proteins were explored using liver transcriptomic analysis, network pharmacology and literature-informed candidate prioritization, followed by preliminary in vivo and in vitro validation. RESULTS: GQD produced heterogeneous anti-hyperglycaemic responses more closely associated with differences in insulin sensitivity-related measurements than with surrogate BCF indices assessed. Hepatic osteopontin (OPN) expression was elevated in T2DM mice and was selectively downregulated in the exploratory strong-responder subgroup. GQD treatment also reduced elevated OPN expression in insulin-resistant HepG2 cells. Serum OPN concentrations were positively correlated with blood glucose, indicating an association between higher OPN levels and poorer glycaemic outcomes. Wogonin and liquiritigenin were associated with OPN downregulation and increased glucose consumption, with PPARα representing a potential yet unconfirmed mechanistic link. CONCLUSION: OPN is associated with GQD treatment-response heterogeneity and may represent a candidate response-associated marker.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of cyclosporine nephrotoxicity in pediatric patients using therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical data.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cyclosporine A (CsA) nephrotoxicity is a dose-limiting toxicity in pediatric immunosuppression, and early identification of children at risk of CsA-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) remains an unmet clinical need. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In retrospective cohorts of CsA-treated inpatients undergoing therapeutic drug monitoring (352 children; 342 adults), a regularized logistic-regression model was compared with six machine-learning classifiers under five feature-selection schemes, three small-sample strategies were evaluated, and adult-child transferability was assessed on 95 aligned features. A 14-variable model was externally validated in an independent pediatric cohort (n = 257). RESULTS: Regularized logistic regression achieved the best discrimination in children (hold-out AUC 0.800) and adults (hold-out AUC 0.956), with complex models overfitting. Adult and pediatric risk architectures differed fundamentally, with transfer AUCs near chance (≈0.6). The 14-variable model retained discrimination on external validation (AUC 0.784, 95% CI 0.656-0.912). CONCLUSIONS: On small clinical datasets, regularization rather than complexity determines predictive performance. We provide an interpretable, TDM-integrated pediatric CsA-AKI model, deployed as an online calculator, supporting early risk stratification in pediatric CsA therapy.

articles.title: Implementation of UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan in Europe.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Uridine diphosphate glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1) genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan presents an individualized dosing strategy that improves patient safety while maintaining therapeutic efficacy. Nonetheless, little is known about its implementation across Europe. This survey-based study provides an overview of UGT1A1 genotype-guided irinotecan dosing practices across Europe and characterizes how institutional, regulatory and practical barriers affect its broader adoption. METHODS: A 41-question survey assessing implementation, best practices and opinions related to UGT1A1 genotyping was distributed to healthcare professionals identified through professional societies and previous publications on pharmacogenetics or irinotecan, as well as through outreach to medical oncology departments and pharmacogenetic laboratories in Europe. The survey was open for participation for 10 weeks from January to March 2026. RESULTS: Of 345 healthcare professionals invited across 34 European countries, 119 (34%) from 107 centres in 27 countries participated. Respondents included clinicians (N = 40), laboratory experts (N = 34), pharmacologists (N = 33) and researchers (N = 12). Eighteen European countries reported varying extents of UGT1A1 genotyping for irinotecan treatment, with extensive pre-treatment implementation currently present in Italy and the Netherlands. Eight countries reported no testing. The most frequently cited drivers of implementation were the presence of clinical guidelines, reimbursement and test availability. UGT1A1 genotyping panels differed considerably across laboratories. CONCLUSIONS: While UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan is increasingly being adopted in Europe, broad and uniform implementation is still limited and thus far unevenly distributed. Achieving European implementation of pre-treatment UGT1A1 genotyping for irinotecan will require the development and publication of clinical guidelines, test availability and coverage of genotyping costs.
authors: European Working Group for the Implementation of UGT1A1 Testing’

articles.title: Repurposing of LSD - a scoping review of current clinical trials.
articles.abstract: LSD was banned in many countries for a very long time and was purchased by users for recreational use on the black market. Since 2014, there has been steady growth in interest in its potential use in treating pain disorders and neuropsychiatric conditions. Consequently, an increasing number of studies on the repurposing of LSD have been conducted; in some cases, the conditions treated corresponded to those in studies from the 1950s and 1960s, while in others, the scope was expanded to include new areas of application. Clinicaltrials.org, ANZCTR, the Netherlands trial registry and PubMed research were used to identify the clinical trials. For this publication, 51 studies were analyzed, 25 of which were published. The goal is to map the status quo of the current state of research and analyze the study design. The analysis parameters included study design, conditions, sponsoring, study location, and overall outcome. Most studies are still in phase 1, followed by phase 2. Three phase 3 studies are currently being conducted. The condition entities were: alcohol use disorder (n = 1), anxiety disorders (n = 3), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) (n = 1), cluster headache (chronic and non-chronic, n = 2); major depressive disorder (n = 4), premenstrual disorders (premenstrual syndrome (PMS)) and Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) (n = 1), palliative care/end-of-life distress (n = 2). The most used dosage is 100 µg. Most studies are interventional RCTs using inactive placebos and are conducted in Switzerland, followed by the USA, the Netherlands, and New Zealand/Australia. The outcome of the published trials was analyzed further. So far, LSD shows possible benefits in the treatment of anxiety disorders and major depressive disorders. The effectiveness of microdosing could not be adequately proven, and the results varied greatly, which could be due to differences in dosage and administration. More detailed studies, particularly phase 2 or phase 3 studies, are needed to make more informed statements.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine-associated bradycardia in perioperative and critical care settings: a cross-database pharmacovigilance study using FAERS and JADER.
articles.abstract: Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist widely used for sedation in perioperative and critical care settings. Although bradycardia is a recognised adverse effect, its temporal reporting patterns and associated clinical characteristics remain incompletely characterised. This study investigated DEX-associated bradycardia using two independent spontaneous reporting systems. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database from 2004Q1 to 2025Q3. Reports suggestive of perioperative or critical care use were identified using predefined proxy indicators. Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect cardiovascular safety signals. Time to onset (TTO) patterns were evaluated using Weibull modelling, and factors associated with bradycardia reporting were examined using multivariable case-non-case logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses assessed the consistency of the findings. Among 2505 DEX reports, 717 involved bradycardia-associated events (FAERS, n = 327; JADER, n = 390). Bradycardia showed prominent disproportionality signals in both databases. Among 198 reports with valid TTO data, the median onset time was 0 days in both databases, with similar Weibull shape parameters (FAERS, β = 0.849; JADER, β = 0.847), suggesting early clustering of reported events. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease showed the strongest adjusted association with bradycardia reporting (OR 4.88, 95% CI 3.92-6.09), followed by concomitant opioid use (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.37-2.22) and β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.08-3.13). These associations were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses. DEX-associated bradycardia showed consistent reporting signals across FAERS and JADER, with reported onset times frequently concentrated near treatment initiation. Cardiovascular disease and concomitant opioid or β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure were associated with higher odds of bradycardia reporting. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish causality or quantify incidence, these findings provide complementary post-marketing evidence supporting careful cardiovascular assessment and haemodynamic monitoring during DEX administration.

articles.title: Exploring candidate molecular links between acetamiprid-related targets and osteosarcoma-associated signatures using network toxicology, transcriptomic analyses, and in vitro validation.
articles.abstract: Acetamiprid (ACE) has been implicated not only in bone metabolic disorders but also in the development of various cancers. Nevertheless, its role in osteosarcoma (OS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, molecular docking, single-cell analysis, machine learning, and preliminary in vitro experiments to explore potential links between ACE-related targets and OS-associated signatures. We identified 219 ACE-related targets and 3299 OS-associated genes, including 62 overlapping candidates. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted inflammatory pathways, including TNF and IL-17 signaling. Exploratory machine learning analyses prioritized CAT and MPO, with CAT showing comparatively more consistent support across subsequent analyses and MPO showing less consistent cross-dataset performance. CAT demonstrated dataset-level discriminatory performance in the evaluated public transcriptomic datasets. Immune-context and single-cell analyses further characterized associations between candidate-gene expression, inferred immune-cell composition, and cellular distribution. Molecular docking generated computationally plausible ACE-protein binding poses but did not establish direct target engagement. In vitro, ACE treatment altered cellular metabolic activity, wound closure, and CAT expression in U-2 OS cells under the tested conditions. CAT emerged as a prioritized candidate molecular feature associated with ACE-related cellular responses and OS-associated molecular signatures. These findings are exploratory and do not establish a causal relationship between ACE exposure and OS development or progression. Further studies using independent tissue cohorts, mechanistic gene perturbation, direct target-engagement assays, and in vivo validation are required.

articles.title: Metronidazole derivatives and phenolic compounds as potential adjuvants against bacterial resistance mediated by the MepA efflux pump in the Staphylococcus aureus K2068 strain.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive pathogen that possesses resistance factors responsible for the occurrence of several diseases, including those affecting the airways and gastrointestinal tract, causing osteomyelitis and systemic infections that increase mortality rates. Metronidazole is a drug with antiparasitic and antibacterial activity, and the phenolic compounds eugenol, dihydroeugenol, guaiacol, and phenol exhibit several therapeutic activities, one of which is antibacterial. Thus, eight compounds were synthesized by linking metronidazole with the aforementioned compounds, forming substances designated AD1-AD8. This study aimed to investigate the adjuvant potential of compounds AD1-AD8 in enhancing the action of ciprofloxacin and ethidium bromide against the S. aureus K2068 strain, considering the possible involvement of MepA efflux pump modulation, as well as to evaluate the direct antibacterial activity of these compounds. Broth microdilution assays and molecular docking studies were performed to assess antibacterial activity and inhibition of the MepA efflux pump. Compounds AD1-AD8 reduced the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of ciprofloxacin and ethidium bromide, with molecular docking results demonstrating a possible inhibition of the MepA efflux pump. Overall, substances AD1-AD8 were able to significantly potentiate the action of the antibiotic and ethidium bromide due to the probable blockade of the resistance mechanism. The obtained results indicate the potential of compounds AD1-AD8 as therapeutic adjuvants in combating efflux pump-mediated bacterial resistance.

articles.title: Associating p-phenylenediamine and p-toluenediamine with AML using a network toxicology-based approach.
articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a prevalent acute hematological malignancy among adults, notable for its unfavorable prognosis and relatively low survival rates. Evidence suggests prolonged exposure to substandard permanent hair dyes containing hazardous chemical agents may elevate cancer risk, including AML. However, the precise mechanisms underlying this carcinogenic association remain elusive. This research identified p-phenylenediamine (PPD) and p-toluenediamine (PTD), primary constituents of hair dyes, as highly carcinogenic substances potentially implicated as key drivers of AML linked to hair dye usage. Targets relevant to PPD and PTD were predicted using databases such as ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, STITCH, and PharmMapper. Additionally, AML-related targets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and GeneCards databases. Core genes were isolated using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis confirmed the predictive accuracy of these critical targets. Immune cell infiltration analysis further elucidated potential associations between these targets and the AML immune microenvironment. To verify compound-target interactions and stability, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted. Our computational predictions suggest that PPD/PTD may directly target PTPRC, suggesting a potential mechanism by which these compounds disrupt immune microenvironment homeostasis and could promote AML progression. These findings suggest that PPD/PTD exposure could promote AML progression, which warrants experimental validation.

articles.title: Real world evidence of second-generation antipsychotics for the management of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This is the first systematic review synthesizing exclusively real-world evidence about the efficacy, acceptability, and tolerability of the most used Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) for the management of Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD). METHODS: Observational or quasi-experimental real-world studies were included involving participants with a mean age of > 50 years and an Alzheimer Disease, vascular dementia or mixed dementia diagnosis with BPSD. Interventions were SGAs. Suitable comparators were placebo, other SGAs or no-treatment. Studies with or without a control group were eligible. The primary outcomes were efficacy, acceptability and tolerability of SGAs for the management of BPSD. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. PROSPERO (CRD420251143630). RESULTS: 17 studies were included, encompassing 7,748 participants. Of the evaluated SGAs, only risperidone (k = 5 studies, n = 1469) and quetiapine (k = 4 studies, n = 89) had sufficient real-world evidence for pre-post analyses. Two studies provided direct comparisons between risperidone and olanzapine. The pooled analysis showed no significant difference between risperidone and olanzapine on efficacy (SMD = - 0.19; 95% CI [ - 1.72, 1.34], I2 = 0%). BPSD appear to improve in pre-post studies with risperidone (SMD = - 1.36; 95% CI [ - 1.67, - 1.06], I2 = 82.1%), but not with quetiapine (MD: - 15.17; 95% CI [-32.18 to 1.84]; I2 = 89.7%). Quality of evidence was evaluated as very low on all outcomes. CONCLUSION: While evidence suggests that risperidone is associated with significant management of BPSD in routine clinical practice, quetiapine appears to show limited efficacy and lower acceptability; although apparent inefficacy may probably depend on small sample size. Despite lower discontinuation rates than those reported in clinical trials, the risks of EPS, falls, and mortality support the need for careful monitoring and individualized risk-benefit assessment. The very low quality of the evidence demands careful interpretation of findings.

articles.title: Jujuboside A from Ziziphus: Chemistry, mechanistic pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and formulation roadmap toward neuroactive translation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Jujuboside A (JuA) is a dammarane-type triterpenoid saponin and a principal quality marker of Ziziphi spinosae semen (ZSS) and selected Ziziphus taxa. OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to integrate current evidence on JuA chemistry, central nervous system (CNS) pharmacology, pharmacokinetics (PK), metabolism, safety, analytical standardization, and formulation strategies toward neuroactive translation. METHODS: Evidence relevant to these domains was synthesized and critically organized to define the chemical, pharmacological, pharmacokinetic, quality-control, and formulation profile of JuA. RESULTS: JuA is characterized by a jujubogenin aglycone linked to a branched oligosaccharide chain, while comparative Ziziphus saponins, including JuB, JuC, protojujubosides, and jujubogenin, clarify how glycosylation influences amphiphilicity, stability, and disposition. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for CNS-related effects, particularly GABAergic modulation, neuroinflammatory restraint, mitochondrial and synaptic protection, and sleep- or stress-linked behavioral outcomes. JuA shows low oral exposure, with an oral bioavailability of approximately 1.32% and rapid stepwise deglycosylation to JuB and jujubogenin, supporting a metabolite-driven pharmacodynamic model. Standardization should integrate authenticated botanical sourcing, ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) or charged-aerosol detection/quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (CAD/qNMR) quantification, chemometric fingerprints, and contaminant controls. Lipid-based systems, cyclodextrin complexes, and amorphous solid dispersions should be evaluated for their capacity to protect labile glycosidic linkages, sustain supersaturation, and improve exposure to pharmacologically relevant species. CONCLUSION: Key priorities are direct receptor engagement, brain-region exposure mapping, PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) alignment, standardized clinical-grade materials, and early human studies using objective sleep endpoints.

articles.title: Recognition and management of semaglutide overdose and intoxi​cation: a narrative review for clinicians.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Semaglutide has moved within a few years from a niche glucose-lowering agent to one of the most widely dispensed medicines in high-income countries, and reported excessive exposures have risen in parallel. This review sets out a practical framework for recognising and managing semaglutide overdose, and distinguishes recommendations supported by published overdose evidence from those resting on pharmacological reasoning or general toxicology practice. EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to July 2026 for English-language human studies of semaglutide pharmacology, safety and excessive exposure, supplemented by reference lists and regulatory agency publications. Randomised trials and meta-analyses were prioritised for statements about incidence; case reports, case series and poison centre or pharmacovigilance analyses informed the description of the overdose syndrome itself. RESULTS: The dominant toxidrome is gastrointestinal and protracted, with nausea, repetitive vomiting, abdominal pain and anorexia persisting for days to weeks because the terminal elimination half-life approaches one week. Volume depletion, electrolyte derangement and acute kidney injury drive serious outcome. Hypoglycaemia is uncommon in isolated overdose because insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent, but it matters with concomitant insulin or sulfonylurea therapy, in non-diabetic individuals, and where a falsified product contains insulin. Pancreatitis, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, ileus and delayed gastric emptying with aspiration risk are less frequent but potentially life-threatening. In the cases reported to date, most exposures follow therapeutic error, unit-conversion confusion with compounded multi-dose vials, and acquisition outside regulated supply. CONCLUSION: Management is supportive and anticipatory. There is no antidote, and extracorporeal removal is futile given extensive albumin binding. Priorities are aggressive antiemesis, fluid and electrolyte correction, glucose monitoring proportionate to risk, full-stomach airway precautions, and observation that respects the drug's long half-life. Prevention through device design, dispensing standards, patient education and regulatory action is likely to yield greater benefit than any therapeutic manoeuvre.

articles.title: Small extracellular vesicle-associated miRNAs in lung cancer: therapeutic potential, drug delivery applications, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Small extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated microRNAs (miRNAs) have attracted interest as regulators of intercellular communication and candidates for lung cancer biomarkers and RNA therapeutics. However, uncertain cellular origin, analytical variability, and limited clinical validation complicate their translation. PURPOSE: To critically assess the biological functions, clinical applications, and translational readiness of EV-associated and exosome-enriched miRNAs in lung cancer. METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, covering publications from January 2017 to June 2026 and supplemented by foundational earlier studies. Evidence was purposively selected according to mechanistic relevance, methodological quality, clinical validation, and translational significance. Findings were synthesized using origin-confidence (OC1-OC3) and evidence-readiness (ER1-ER4) frameworks. RESULTS: EV-associated miRNAs were implicated in tumor-stromal communication, endothelial barrier disruption, metastasis, and treatment resistance. Of 11 patient-linked biomarker studies, ten analyzed total circulating EV fractions (OC1), while one used tumor-associated EV enrichment (OC2); patient samples did not verify a direct malignant-cell origin. Two diagnostic studies included independent external validation (ER3). Experimental studies supported EV-mediated transfer of gefitinib resistance-associated miR-214 and antimetastatic activity of miR-126-loaded EVs in vivo. Variability in EV isolation, hemolysis assessment, miRNA normalization, and clinical validation limited cross-study comparability. CONCLUSION: EV-associated miRNAs offer potential for lung cancer risk stratification, treatment monitoring, and therapeutic delivery. Clinical translation requires standardized vesicle characterization, independent prospective validation, and quantitative assessment of delivery efficiency, biodistribution, and safety.

articles.title: Chronopharmaceutics of In Situ Gel-Based Drug Delivery Systems in the Treatment of Nocturnal Asthma: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nocturnal asthma (NA) is characterized by airway resistance and inflammation that peak between 02:00 and 06:00, driven by circadian fluctuations in vagal tone, cortisol, and inflammatory mediators. Conventional inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β₂-agonist combinations and oral therapies may not reliably cover this window because of suboptimal adherence, heterogeneous lung deposition, and variable systemic exposure after oral dosing. In situ gels (ISGs), which are liquids that gel after administration, have been proposed as platforms for sustained nasal or pulmonary drug delivery. OBJECTIVE: To review the circadian mechanisms of NA, the formulation science of stimuli-responsive ISGs, and the evidence for their use as chronotherapeutic systems in NA. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes literature on the molecular clock and circadian pathophysiology of asthma, polymer selection and gelation mechanisms, nasal and pulmonary delivery, pharmacokinetics and safety, and manufacturing and regulatory considerations. Evidence was classified by type (in vitro or ex vivo, animal, computational, or human) and as established, preclinical, or hypothetical. RESULTS: Thermosensitive poloxamers, pH-responsive carbopol/chitosan systems, ion-activated gellan gum, and enzyme-degradable matrices can form mucoadhesive depots, but their gelation behaviour, mechanical stability, mucociliary clearance, and tolerability depend on formulation composition and test conditions. Hybrid architectures (nanoparticle-embedded, nanomicelle-forming, and mesoporous silica ISGs) may allow release kinetics to be separated from cellular uptake. Sustained release over several hours has been shown for gel formulations in vitro. No study has evaluated a chronotherapeutic ISG in nocturnal asthma, and benefits for airway function and adherence remain undemonstrated. Afternoon or evening dosing of inhaled corticosteroids has clinical trial support and is the main alternative chronotherapeutic strategy. Data on repeated nightly dosing and on bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration are lacking. CONCLUSION: Chronotherapeutic ISGs are a plausible but untested approach to nocturnal asthma. Priorities for translation are studies that measure drug exposure across the 02:00-06:00 window, bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration, and the safety of repeated nightly dosing. Regulatory, manufacturing, biomarker-responsive, and digital-integration concepts remain exploratory.

articles.title: Examining the Safety Profile of Amitriptyline Versus Placebo and Active Comparators in the Elderly: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Amitriptyline remains in use among older adults despite safety concerns. This diagnosis-independent systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated amitriptyline safety and tolerability versus active comparators or placebo in older adults. DATA SOURCES: We searched MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Embase, PsycINFO, ClinicalTrials.gov, and World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP) through September 30, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) compared amitriptyline with placebo or active comparators in older adults (participants aged ≥60 years or study populations with mean age ≥70 years). Primary outcomes included serious adverse events (SAEs), dizziness, and acute cognitive adverse outcomes. Secondary outcomes included 60 safety, tolerability, and acceptability outcomes. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were calculated. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately versus placebo and active comparators on an intention-to-treat basis. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored robustness. DATA SYNTHESIS: In total, 32 RCTs (2243 participants) were included. Versus active comparators, that is, antidepressants or mood stabilizers, amitriptyline did not increase serious adverse events (SAEs) (RR = 1.13; 95% CI, 0.66-1.93), but increased dizziness (RR = 1.38; 95% CI, 1.06-1.79). Regarding cognition, no difference was found for disturbance in attention (RR = 2.44; 95% CI, 0.89-6.71) or confusional state (RR = 1.76; 95% CI, 0.42-7.35); disorientation was reported in 1 trial. Amitriptyline was associated with increased risk of any adverse event, withdrawals due to adverse events, anticholinergic and sedative adverse events, and weight gain. Placebo-controlled data were sparse, with no SAEs reported. Limitations included short trials, sparse adverse event reporting, and restricted eligibility. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: Amitriptyline's main limitation in older adults may be tolerability rather than excess serious harm. It should not be a first-line option, but may remain reasonable for selected patients with clear therapeutic rationale. CONCLUSION: Compared with active comparators, amitriptyline showed no detectable excess in SAEs but increased dizziness and anticholinergic and sedative adverse events.

articles.title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD. METHODS: A MAFLD mouse model was established by administration of a high-fat diet. Serum biochemical parameters were measured, and liver histopathological injury was assessed by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson staining. Hepatocyte apoptosis was evaluated using TUNEL staining. Oxidative stress markers were quantified using ELISA, flow cytometry, and DCFH-DA staining, respectively. Cell viability and apoptosis were assessed by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay and flow cytometry. Intracellular Fe²⁺ and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels were measured using commercial assay kits. The acetylation level of the SREBP1 promoter was determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation. RESULTS: BGN4 significantly alleviated liver injury, oxidative stress, and hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD mice. BGN4 treatment markedly increased the level of the intestinal metabolite 6-HNA. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that 6-HNA exerted a protective effect against palmitic acid (PA)-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress. Mechanistically, 6-HNA activated Nrf2 signaling, thereby suppressing the SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis through reduction of p300-mediated histone acetylation. Rescue experiments showed that treatment with ML-385 or overexpression of SREBP1 reversed the protective effects of 6-HNA on PA-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that the protective effects of BGN4 against hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress in MAFLD are likely associated with the upregulation of intestinal metabolite 6-HNA, which appears to modulate the Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 signaling axis, thereby supporting the therapeutic potential of the "probiotic-metabolite-liver" regulatory axis in MAFLD.

articles.title: Combined effects of aerobic interval training and hesperidin supplementation on inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in a rat model of paclitaxel-induced neuropathy: evidence for additive therapeutic effects.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CINP) is characterized by numbness, pain, and motor dysfunction, primarily in the extremities. It is a common and debilitating side effect of paclitaxel, an antineoplastic agent with clinical uses in several malignancies, including tumors of the breast, ovary, prostate, and lung. Despite ongoing research, effective therapies for CINP remain limited. Thus, this preclinical study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of aerobic interval exercise (EX) with/without hesperidin (HES) on paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain in rats. METHODS: Thirty male Wistar rats were randomly divided into five groups (n = 6): sham, paclitaxel (PTX), PTX with exercise (EX), PTX with HES (100 mg/kg), and PTX with EX and HES. PTX (2 mg/kg) was injected intraperitoneally on days 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 of the study protocol. HES (100 mg/kg) was administered orally 5 days/week (days 14-35). The exercise training protocol (7 min running at 13-16 m/min, 5 days/week) was initiated after a 1-week acclimation period (day - 7) and continued throughout the study. Mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia tests were conducted at 8 time points: baseline (day - 14) and on days - 7, 0, 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35 to evaluate the rats' response to treatment. The animals were finally sacrificed, and their spinal cord tissues were used to determine the expression levels of several inflammatory and oxidative stress cytokines, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α, malondialdehyde, and glutathione. RESULTS: Treatment with EX or HES alone significantly decreased mechanical allodynia (paw withdrawal threshold increased; p < 0.01) and thermal hyperalgesia (withdrawal latency increased; p < 0.001). Combined EX + HES treatment showed enhanced effects, with further improvements in both mechanical allodynia (p < 0.001 vs. either treatment alone) and thermal hyperalgesia (p < 0.001 vs. either treatment alone). The PTX-induced weight loss was significantly attenuated by EX (p < 0.01) and HES (p < 0.05), with the combination showing additive effects (p < 0.001 vs. PTX). Regarding biochemical markers, EX + HES combination demonstrated significant reduction in inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress markers, while synergistically increasing anti-inflammatory and antioxidant markers. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the hypothesis that treadmill exercise with/without HES suppresses neuropathic pain and inflammatory and oxidative stress factors strongly affected by chemotherapies. Thus, this therapeutic protocol might be an alternative candidate for the management of paclitaxel-induced neuropathy. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Modulation of lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181 and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1 signaling pathways in rotenone-induced neurodegeneration rat model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss and α-synuclein-rich Lewy body accumulation. Mitochondrial dysfunction and microRNA (miRNA) dysregulation, particularly mitochondrial miRNAs (mitomiRs), are critical drivers of PD pathogenesis. METHODS: This study investigated the neuroprotective efficacy of the SGLT2 inhibitor, dapagliflozin, against rotenone-induced neurotoxicity, focusing on the lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK signaling axes. Male Wistar rats were randomized into three groups: a control group, a PD model group received rotenone (2 mg/kg every 48 h, s.c.), and a treatment group received rotenone plus dapagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day, p.o.) for 28 days. RESULTS: In the inducted rotenone group lincRNA-p21 sponges mir-181 which leads to the upregulation of PTEN which inhibits the conversion of PIP2 to PIP3 thus downregulating AKT expression and subsequent activation of GSK-3β kinase enzyme which increases α-synuclein accumulation. In addition, the PD-control group showed upregulation of Mitomir-23b with subsequent downregulation of SIRT-1 expression and inactivation of LKB1. Accompanied by inhibition of AMPK phosphorylation which in turn prevents the degradation of accumulated α-synuclein. Dapagliflozin treatment upregulates mir-181 and downregulates mitomir-23b, which restores DJ-1 levels, which in turn activate the antioxidant genes HO-1 and PINK1, and improve mitochondrial function. CONCLUSIONS: Dapagliflozin exerts neuroprotection by restoring lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK homeostasis, thereby inhibiting α-synuclein proteotoxicity and mitigating oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.

articles.title: A Weight of Evidence Framework to Replace Repeat-Dose Inhalation Study for Crop Protection Products.
articles.abstract: This paper presents a tiered weight-of-evidence framework for waiving repeat-dose inhalation toxicity studies while maintaining scientific rigor in pesticide risk assessment. The approach first evaluates the potential for portal of entry effects using acute toxicity data, QSAR models, and relevant in vitro assays. Where portal of entry effects are indicated, in vitro points of departure can be combined with inhalation dosimetry to derive protective endpoints. Where such effects are not expected, an exposure-based waiver approach is evaluated first. If the margin of exposure is inadequate, a comparative pharmacokinetic assessment, supported by minimal in vivo data and computational modeling, can be used to extrapolate oral toxicity endpoints to inhalation-equivalent values. By integrating new approach methodologies, exposure information, and route-to-route extrapolation, the framework provides a practical path to reduce reliance on traditional animal inhalation studies while maintaining human health protection. It aligns with current regulatory flexibility, supports the 3Rs principles of reduction, replacement, and refinement, and can incorporate future advances in in vitro and in silico tools. This framework lays the groundwork for broader replacement of repeat-dose inhalation studies in pesticide risk assessment.

Unmasking Hidden Risks in Herbal Weight-Loss Supplements: LC-MS/MS - Based Detection of Sibutramine Adulteration for Consumer Safety Assessment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Herbal weight-loss supplements are widely perceived as safe alternatives to synthetic drugs; however, illegal adulteration with undeclared pharmaceuticals remains a significant public health concern. Sibutramine, withdrawn from the market because of serious cardiovascular risks, is one of the most frequently detected adulterants. This study aimed to develop and validate a sensitive liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method to detection of sibutramine in herbal dietary supplements, and to evaluate the presence of sibutramine in commercially available some of the selected products. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed sibutramine by ultra high-performance LC-MS/MS using a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with electrospray ionization in multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode. Identification was based on the protonated precursor ion (m/z 280) and characteristic product-ion transitions. The method was validated for linearity, limits of detection and quantification, recovery, accuracy, precision, robustness, and matrix effects in accordance with internationally accepted bioanalytical validation guidelines. RESULTS: The method demonstrated excellent linearity over the range of 5-500 µg/L (r2 = 0.99987), with detection and quantification limits of 0.82 µg/L and 2.73 µg/L, respectively. Validation demonstrated satisfactory accuracy, precision, recovery, robustness, and negligible matrix effects, confirming the method's suitability for routine analysis. Analysis of 17 commercially available herbal weight-loss supplements revealed the presence of sibutramine in 15 samples (88%), with concentrations ranging from trace levels to substantial amounts, indicating widespread adulteration. CONCLUSION: The validated LC-MS/MS method provides a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for routine monitoring of sibutramine in herbal dietary supplements. The high prevalence of sibutramine detected in marketed products highlights the persistent problem of illegal adulteration and underscores the need for continuous market surveillance, stricter regulatory enforcement, and routine analytical screening to safeguard public health and ensure product quality.
